title: [bug] cloudwatch CBOR path treats a body-read failure as an empty body
notes:
Found 2026-08-22 by the gopherstack-ifzn matcher sweep, documented in
services/cloudwatch/PARITY.md rather than fixed, because it is a different
path from the one that sweep was fixing.

handleTargetRequest on the CBOR path does not distinguish a ReadBody FAILURE
from an empty body. An oversized or unreadable request is processed as though
the client sent nothing, so the caller gets whatever an empty request produces
rather than an error saying the body could not be read.

THIS IS THE LIVE PATH, WHICH IS WHY IT MATTERS. cloudwatch's pinned SDK
(v1.66.3) uses rpcv2.NewCBOR exclusively -- verified, api_client.go. The
form-urlencoded branch fixed under ifzn is reachable only by a raw request; the
CBOR branch is what every real Go client actually hits.

RELATED PRIOR ART, and the reason this shape keeps appearing: pkgs/httputils
ReadBody now caches a read FAILURE as well as a success (see the
gopherstack-3a8t commit), so a handler can no longer accidentally re-read and
get a short body with a nil error. Check whether this path predates that or
simply ignores the returned error.

Note also that cloudwatch's XML path was found live earlier today
(gopherstack-jodk): DeleteDashboards omitted its Result node, and the pinned
client speaks CBOR, so "no pinned client speaks this protocol" does NOT mean
"no client does". Fix the error handling on the CBOR path without assuming the
other paths are dead.

PROOF STANDARD: a real SDK client -- which will speak CBOR -- sending an
oversized body, asserting a typed error rather than whatever the empty-request
path returns. A status assertion alone will not catch this, since an empty
request may well also produce a 400.

Related: gopherstack-ifzn, gopherstack-3a8t, gopherstack-wlo1.
close_reason: Closed

title: docdb/neptune RouteMatcher can't safely claim-on-read-failure until Handler()/ExtractOperation stop using r.ParseForm()
notes:
Found 2026-08-22 while fixing gopherstack-3a8t (elasticache RouteMatcher
swallowing a body-read failure as a 404).

docdb and neptune are the only 2 of 17 body-reading RouteMatchers that already
narrow ownership via a body-independent signal before reading the body
(service.MatchesUserAgentMarker(r.Header, "api/docdb"/"api/neptune"), verified
against the real AddSDKAgentKeyValue call in the pinned aws-sdk-go-v2 SDKs) --
so, unlike the other 15, they could safely change RouteMatcher's
ReadBody-failure branch from `return false` to `return true` without
misrouting a sibling service's oversized-body request to themselves.

I tried exactly that fix and it does NOT work: both services' Handler(),
ExtractOperation, and ExtractResource call r.ParseForm() directly (not
httputils.ReadBody). net/http's own ParseForm() caches r.PostForm as a
non-nil-but-empty map on its FIRST failed call (see net/http's ParseForm:
`if r.PostForm == nil { r.PostForm = make(url.Values) }` runs even when
parsePostForm returned an error). The telemetry wrapper calls
observer.ExtractOperation(c) BEFORE the service's own Handler() runs
(pkgs/telemetry/echo_wrapper.go), so ExtractOperation's ParseForm() call hits
the read failure first and poisons r.PostForm/r.Form to empty; Handler()'s
own ParseForm() call then sees r.PostForm already non-nil and skips
re-parsing entirely, silently returning nil (no error) with an empty form.
Result: Handler() sees Action == "" and answers MissingAction instead of the
InternalFailure it should produce for an unreadable body.

Proved this concretely: wrote TestHandler_OversizedBodySurfacesInternalFailure
for both services (same shape as elasticache's, driving a real SDK client
through service.NewRegistry/NewServiceRouter) with the matcher fix applied --
both failed with "MissingAction" instead of "InternalFailure". Reverted the
matcher fix and deleted those tests rather than ship a fix proven broken.

THE FIX: migrate docdb's and neptune's three ParseForm() call sites
(ExtractOperation, ExtractResource, Handler(), each in services/docdb/handler.go
and services/neptune/handler.go) to use httputils.ReadBody + url.ParseQuery,
mirroring elasticache's own pattern exactly -- httputils.ReadBody was hardened
in gopherstack-3a8t to cache a read failure the same way it already cached a
success, so repeat calls return the identical error deterministically. Once
that migration lands, RouteMatcher's ReadBody-failure branch can safely change
from `return false` to `return true` (the User-Agent check already above it
in both matchers establishes ownership).

Verify no other ParseForm() double-read landmines exist for these two
services beyond the three call sites found (grep confirmed exactly 3 each as
of this writing).
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] elasticache RouteMatcher swallows a body-read failure and 404s instead of routing
notes:
Found 2026-08-22 while fixing gopherstack-o7gx. It MASKED that bug in
elasticache and had to be worked around to write the test at all.

THE SHAPE. elasticache's RouteMatcher calls httputils.ReadBody to inspect the
form body and decide whether the request belongs to this service. On a read
failure -- oversized body, read error -- it returns false rather than
surfacing the error. The router then finds no owner and answers 404.

So an oversized elasticache request never reaches Handler() at all. The
caller gets a 404 saying the resource does not exist, when the truth is that
the body was too large to read. Wrong status, wrong meaning, and it hides
whatever the handler would have said.

HOW IT WAS FOUND. The o7gx test for elasticache is an oversized body driven
through a real SDK client. It kept returning 404/UnknownError rather than the
handler's error, because routing consumed the failure first. The committed
test mounts the handler directly (e.Any("/*", h.Handler()), an established
pattern in cleanrooms and iot tests) to get past routing -- a deliberate
workaround, recorded here rather than left as a mystery for the next reader.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE SERVICE. A RouteMatcher that inspects the body to
claim a request is a design several services may share. Check whether any
other matcher reads the body and swallows the error the same way. The
gopherstack-6flj RouteMatcher prefix-collision work is the nearest precedent
for how these interact, and its lesson stands: do NOT fix this by raising
MatchPriority.

THE FIX IS A DESIGN QUESTION, not a rename, which is why this is filed rather
than patched. A matcher cannot return an error today. Options: have it claim
the request and let the handler produce the typed error (probably right, since
the handler already does this correctly after o7gx); or give matchers a way to
signal "mine, but unreadable". Decide before coding.

PROOF STANDARD: an oversized elasticache request through a real SDK client,
routed normally, asserting the handler's InternalFailure rather than a 404.
The existing o7gx test already proves the handler half; this needs the routing
half, without the direct-mount workaround.

Related: gopherstack-o7gx, gopherstack-6flj.
Fixed elasticache (uncommitted, awaiting orchestrator review/commit): RouteMatcher's
ReadBody-failure branch now falls back to service.MatchesUserAgentMarker(r.Header,
"api/elasticache") (verified against pinned elasticache@v1.56.4 api_client.go:637's
AddSDKAgentKeyValue call) instead of unconditionally returning false, letting Handler()
produce its already-typed InternalFailure (gopherstack-o7gx) instead of a masking 404.
Also hardened httputils.ReadBody to cache a read failure the same way it already cached
a success (new bodyReadErrCloser), so repeated ReadBody calls on the same request return
the identical error instead of silently succeeding on a truncated re-read.

Survey: 17 of 162 services' RouteMatchers read the body and swallow a read failure as
false/404 (elbv2, rds, sqs, autoscaling, elasticbeanstalk, cloudwatch, ses, iam,
elasticache, sts, ec2, docdb, cloudformation, elb, neptune, sns, redshift) -- full detail
in services/elasticache/PARITY.md's 2026-08-22 entry.

Design rejected: claiming unconditionally on read failure, for any of the other 16 --
verified these 17 are structurally indistinguishable from each other (form-urlencoded
POST) without reading the body, so claiming on failure would misrouted an oversized body
to whichever sibling sorts first by MatchPriority (STS) rather than to its real target.

Rejected mid-fix: extending the same claim-on-failure change to docdb/neptune (the only
other 2 of the 17 with a body-independent User-Agent check already in RouteMatcher). Their
Handler()/ExtractOperation/ExtractResource use r.ParseForm() directly rather than
httputils.ReadBody; net/http's own ParseForm() caches an empty-but-non-nil r.PostForm after
its first failed call, and the telemetry wrapper calls ExtractOperation before Handler(),
so Handler()'s own ParseForm() call silently "succeeds" empty on the second call --
verified this concretely (wrote the same test, got MissingAction instead of
InternalFailure), then reverted rather than ship it broken. Filed gopherstack-bahs
(docdb/neptune, blocked on migrating those 3 call sites/service to httputils.ReadBody)
and gopherstack-ifzn (remaining 13, each needs its own verified User-Agent marker) as
follow-ups.

Proof: TestHandler_OversizedBodySurfacesInternalFailure in
services/elasticache/handler_oversized_body_test.go now drives a real SDK client through
service.NewRegistry/NewServiceRouter (dropped the direct-Handler()-mount workaround from
gopherstack-o7gx), confirmed failing pre-fix with UnknownError instead of InternalFailure.
TestHandler_NormalSizedBodyStillRoutes added as the regression guard.

Files touched (uncommitted): pkgs/httputils/httputils.go,
services/elasticache/handler.go, services/elasticache/handler_oversized_body_test.go,
services/elasticache/PARITY.md.

Gates run clean: go build ./..., go vet (+e2e/integration tags via make build-check),
gofmt -l (empty), go test -race ./pkgs/httputils/... ./services/elasticache/...,
golangci-lint run ./pkgs/httputils/... ./services/elasticache/... (0 issues).
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] ReadBody-failure paths write untyped errors in 27 services
notes:
Named but not fixed by the gopherstack-wlo1 sweep that produced c6554e9f8.
Same class, same signature, a bounded and enumerated list.

THE SHAPE. httputils.ReadBody(...) fails -- body too large, read error -- and
the handler answers with a bare c.String(http.StatusBadRequest, ...) or
c.String(http.StatusInternalServerError, ...). Plain text. Every JSON-protocol
deserializer parses errors through restjson.GetErrorInfo, which JSON-decodes
the body, so plain text does not decode at all.

That is worse than the UnknownError outcome this class usually produces. When
pkgs/service.HandleTarget had the identical defect, the hand-revert produced
*json.SyntaxError -- "invalid character 'M' looking for beginning of value".
The SDK cannot construct a GenericAPIError from a body it cannot parse, so the
caller gets a decode failure rather than an API error.

THE 27, each protocol-classified by the sweep that found them: apigateway (a
DIFFERENT site from the one fixed in c6554e9f8 -- its top-level handleRESTAPI
and decodeRequest paths), appsync, cleanrooms, databrew, dynamodbstreams,
elasticache, grafana, kinesis, mgn, networkmanager, networkmonitor, outposts,
personalize, pipes, ram, rdsdata, redshiftdata, resiliencehub, resourcegroups,
s3tables, sagemaker, scheduler, serverlessrepo, servicediscovery, shield,
timestreamquery, wafv2, xray.

All are restjson1 or awsjson1.0/1.1 EXCEPT elasticache, which is Query/XML and
therefore needs the wrapped ErrorResponse form, not a JSON envelope. Do not
apply one fix to all 27.

WHY THIS SURVIVES. The genuine per-operation error paths in these services are
already correctly typed -- verified repeatedly across iot, vpclattice,
medialive, mediatailor and the HandleTarget case. Only the framework-level and
read-failure paths are mute. That asymmetry is the signature: the obvious path
looks right, so nobody checks the other one.

Nor do tests catch it. A handler test asserting a 400 passes regardless, and a
raw-body test asserts the key its author typed -- which in iot's case was the
wrong one, and a test did exactly that.

DO NOT INVENT AN EXCEPTION TYPE. mediapackage models no 400-class exception at
all, so UnprocessableEntityException was the correct reuse there. Check what
each service actually models before choosing a code.

PROOF STANDARD: a real-SDK-client assertion that ErrorCode() returns the
intended code rather than UnknownError. A status-code assertion cannot see
this class. Some of these paths cannot be reached by any legitimate SDK input;
the technique that worked is a smithy middleware corrupting the request after
signing, or an oversized body.

Related: gopherstack-wlo1.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] error envelopes are wire shape too, and no sweep has ever checked them
notes:
CONFIRMED TWICE IN ONE DAY, in two different protocols, each time affecting
EVERY operation of the service. Neither was found by a sweep -- both fell out
of unrelated work.

  s3control (fixed cfa37cc44): writeXMLErrorCode emitted ProtocolRestXML's
  bare <Error><Code>, the data-plane S3 shape. All 97 of s3control's
  deserializeOpError functions call GetErrorResponseComponents with
  IsWrappedWithErrorTag true, requiring Code and Message nested under a
  wrapping ErrorResponse root. Verified: 97 functions, 97 wrapped. Every
  failure of every op reached a real client as
  smithy.GenericAPIError{Code:"UnknownError"}.

  iot (fixed 099a242bd): roughly 48 malformed-body sites wrote {"error": msg}.
  smithy-go's restjson decoder (aws-sdk-go-v2@v1.43.4
  aws/protocol/restjson/decoder_util.go) recognises __type, code and message.
  There is no "error" key in it. Same outcome: UnknownError, message
  discarded.

WHY NO EXISTING INSTRUMENT FINDS THIS. cmd/keycheck compares SUCCESS response
keys against deserializeOpDocument<Op>Output case lists. The error path is a
different deserializer (deserializeOpError<Op>) and a different runtime helper
entirely. The required-output sweep, the struct-tag sweep and the wrapper-key
campaign all likewise looked only at success shapes. So this surface has been
invisible to every pass this campaign has run.

It is also invisible to tests: a handler test asserting a 400 status passes,
and a raw-body test asserts the key its author typed -- which in iot's case
was the wrong one, and a test did exactly that (fixed in 099a242bd, the
seventh defect-ratifying test found this session).

THE CHECK, per service:
  1. Determine the protocol from the pinned SDK's own deserializer prefix,
     NOT from services/_PROTOCOLS.md -- one of its hand-checked rows was
     already found wrong.
  2. Read what that protocol's error path actually parses:
     - restjson/restxml: smithy-go's protocol helper (restjson.GetErrorInfo
       reads the X-Amzn-ErrorType header first, then __type/code/message in
       the body).
     - awsjson1.0/1.1: __type and message.
     - query/XML: the wrapped ErrorResponse > Error > Code/Message form, and
       note s3's DATA PLANE uses the bare form -- the two are different and
       s3control needs the wrapped one.
  3. Compare against every site the service writes an error body, including
     the malformed-request path. iot's real backend-error path was already
     correct; only the malformed path was mute, which is why nothing noticed.

SIZING: unknown, deliberately not guessed. Two services confirmed out of two
examined by accident, which says nothing reliable about the rest -- but it is
not a reassuring ratio.

PROOF STANDARD: assert through the real SDK client that ErrorCode() returns
the intended code, not UnknownError. A status-code assertion cannot catch
this class, and neither can a raw-body string match.

Related: gopherstack-zquj, gopherstack-n3zi.
ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION, 2026-08-23.

Independently confirmed the ledger was stale: git log --all --grep=wlo1 returns 12 commits, and this issue's notes reflected almost none of them. bd's updated_at sat 57 seconds after the iot fix and BEFORE every other commit in the family. That is the second materially-wrong-in-the-optimistic-direction ledger this session, after jqh2 and enpq.

Spot-verified two of the agent's not-a-bug findings rather than taking them:
  - restjson.GetErrorInfo exists at aws/protocol/restjson/decoder_util.go:15 as cited
  - efs sets X-Amzn-Errortype and its own tests assert it, so the body's non-standard ErrorCode key is never consulted -- deserializeOpError reads the header first

MEASURED YIELD, and it is a null result worth recording precisely.

  method:      signature scan across the 102 unswept services
  raw hits:    ~165 (bare c.String fallbacks, single-key message maps,
               dispatch-miss text, non-standard field names, hand-rolled dispatch)
  real bugs:   0

Every hit was the already-triaged 'marshal cannot fail' fallback, a non-smithy surface (sns raw PEM, apigatewayv2 proxy), or resolved false on reading context.

SO SIGNATURE SCANNING IS NOW A DEAD CLASS, joining owner-scoping, fabricated enums, over-strict validators, json-dash-blocks-ingest and AST decode-struct diff in gopherstack-n3zi. Five of six mechanical classes have produced nothing. The distinguishing property holds: every dead class matches on a NAME, LITERAL or TAG; the two productive ones diff an op against ITS OWN SDK shape.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY STILL OPEN, stated plainly so nobody reads this as done:
  - 60 of 162 services examined by per-op deserializer diff
  - 102 NOT examined that way -- 47 of them route through service.HandleTarget
    so their dispatch-miss path is covered by c6554e9f8, and 2 (qldb,
    qldbsession) have no SDK client at all, leaving 53 restjson1 services
    routed by REST path that are NOT independently confirmed clean
  - cloudwatch's classic Query surface has no deserializers.go and was not checked

The agent's own protocol census corrected a real classifier bug: taking the alphabetically-first SDK import in a directory misclassifies sagemaker and resiliencehub, which each import two SDK packages. Worth knowing for any future census.

RECOMMENDATION: do not run another signature scan on this family. If it is worked again, it must be per-op deserializer diffs on the 53, and that is a real pass, not a sweep.
IDEMPOTENT-DELETE INFERENCE IS NOW DOCUMENTED, 2026-08-23.

Five deletes today returned a not-found code their own op switch cannot type. Each was fixed to succeed instead, on the reasoning that a delete which cannot report not-found must be idempotent. I labelled the first three as INFERENCES, deliberately, because absence of a case is not documentation:

  apigatewayv2 DeletePortal
  codeartifact DeleteDomain
  cleanrooms   DeleteCollaboration

codecommit then supplied AWS's own words, in the SDK doc comments:

  DeleteApprovalRuleTemplate     'has been previously deleted, the only response is a 200 OK'
  DeletePullRequestApprovalRule  'the response is 200 OK without content'

So the pattern is real and documented, not merely plausible. Two further supports:
  - codeartifact's OWN sibling DeleteRepository DOES model ResourceNotFoundException, so the omission on DeleteDomain is per-op and deliberate rather than a modelling gap
  - DeleteSyncConfiguration had the same shape in codeconnections AND codestarconnections independently

RULE FOR THE REST OF THIS SWEEP: when a delete op's switch omits every not-found code, treat idempotent-success as the default reading, and say whether the specific op is documented or inferred.

THE INVERSE DOES NOT HOLD, and this is the part to not get wrong. A GET whose switch omits not-found is NOT idempotent -- there is no sensible success response when the output declares a required field. Two such were filed unfixed rather than guessed: gopherstack-q2yu (bedrockruntime GetAsyncInvoke) and gopherstack-0tid (cleanrooms Get/UpdateCollaboration). Do not 'apply the delete pattern' to them.

Running totals for this issue: 239 ops diffed before this batch, 16 bugs; this batch added 15 more fixes across cloudtrail, codecommit, codeconnections and codestarconnections, including a DashboardNotFoundException typed by ZERO ops in the entire cloudtrail SDK.

which lands 57s after that commit and BEFORE every commit below. None of this

  099a242bd iot (12:10)

(not services/_PROTOCOLS.md): the "19 of 19" Query/XML/ec2query claim is

cloudformation, docdb, elasticache, elasticbeanstalk, elb, elbv2, iam,

THIS SESSION'S PASS (no code changes, zero new bugs). Built the true
examined set from the commits above (60 of 162 services), then ran a
signature scan -- not a full per-op deserializer diff -- across all 102
remaining, using every signature this class has actually produced a real bug
under: bare c.String(http.Status...) fallbacks, single-key {"message":...}
maps with no code/type sibling, dispatch-miss/"unknown operation" text, and
non-__type/code/message field names. Zero new confirmed bugs.

  - 18 services matched the raw c.String pattern. All but 2 are the

title: cognitoidp AssociateSoftwareToken/VerifySoftwareToken/SetUserMFAPreference Session-based flow entirely unimplemented
description:
Real Cognito's AssociateSoftwareTokenInput/VerifySoftwareTokenInput document
Session as an ALTERNATE identifier to AccessToken ("You can provide either an
access token or a session ID in the request" -- api_op_AssociateSoftwareToken.go,
api_op_VerifySoftwareToken.go). This is the real, documented flow for
first-time MFA setup during sign-in: InitiateAuth/RespondToAuthChallenge
returns an MFA_SETUP challenge with a Session token, and the client is meant
to continue AssociateSoftwareToken/VerifySoftwareToken using that Session
alone, with no access token yet (the user isn't fully authenticated until
MFA setup completes).

gopherstack's winning handlers (handleAssociateSoftwareTokenAccurate,
handleVerifySoftwareTokenAccurate in handler_mfa.go, confirmed live via
dispatchTable()'s maps.Copy override order -- see gopherstack-zquj's note
on the OpsA/OpsB/OpsC blind-spot-#6 refinement) only resolve the user via
h.Backend.AssociateSoftwareToken(accessToken)/VerifySoftwareToken(accessToken,
code), both of which call findUserByAccessTokenLocked -- there is no
session-based lookup anywhere in the backend. A real client using the
documented Session-only flow (no AccessToken) gets "not authorized" instead
of completing MFA setup.

The wire-side json tags already declare Session correctly
(associateSoftwareTokenAccurateOutput.Session, verifySoftwareTokenAccurateOutput.Session,
models_mfa.go) -- they are simply never populated because there is nothing
to populate them from.

NOT a key/tag fix: needs a session-token continuation mechanism (mapping a
Session ID back to the in-flight auth challenge's user, as auth_challenges.go
already does for RespondToAuthChallenge) threaded into AssociateSoftwareToken/
VerifySoftwareToken/SetUserMFAPreference. Filed rather than fixed per
gopherstack-zquj's "do not restructure" constraint.
close_reason: Closed

title: cognitoidp SchemaAttribute flattens Number/StringAttributeConstraints -- every real client drops schema min/max
description:
services/cognitoidp/models_attributes.go's SchemaAttribute writes
StringAttributeMinLength/StringAttributeMaxLength (as int64) and
NumberAttributeMinValue/NumberAttributeMaxValue (as float64) as TOP-LEVEL
keys. The real SDK (cognitoidentityprovider@v1.67.4) nests these one level
deeper as string-valued sub-objects: SchemaAttributeType.StringAttributeConstraints
{MinLength,MaxLength *string} and .NumberAttributeConstraints{MinValue,MaxValue
*string} (deserializers.go case "StringAttributeConstraints"/
"NumberAttributeConstraints" in awsAwsjson11_deserializeDocumentSchemaAttributeType,
sub-deserializers at case "MaxLength"/"MinLength" and case "MaxValue" resp.).

Every real client's schema attribute constraints therefore decode as
nil/unset on CreateUserPool, DescribeUserPool, UpdateUserPool, and
ListUserPools (which reuses the same struct) -- this is what keycheck flagged
as StringAttributeMinLength/MaxLength/NumberAttributeMinValue/MaxValue
"not in real reachable shape" (4 mismatches each on CreateUserPool and
DescribeUserPool in the gopherstack-zquj re-sweep).

NOT a pure key/tag fix: needs two new nested struct types
(numberAttributeConstraintsJSON{MinValue,MaxValue string}, stringAttributeConstraintsJSON
{MinLength,MaxLength string}), with values as STRINGS (not int64/float64) per
the real SDK, threaded through SchemaAttribute's json marshaling and every
caller that currently reads/writes the flat fields. Filed rather than fixed
per gopherstack-zquj's "do not restructure" constraint.
close_reason: Closed

title: kafka GetCompatibleKafkaVersions returns the wrong item shape entirely -- structural, not a tag fix
description:
Real GetCompatibleKafkaVersionsOutput.compatibleKafkaVersions is a list of CompatibleKafkaVersion{sourceVersion, targetVersions[]} (deserializers.go's awsRestjson1_deserializeDocumentCompatibleKafkaVersion, kafka SDK) -- grouped by the version you're upgrading FROM, with the list of versions you can upgrade TO. gopherstack's Backend.GetCompatibleKafkaVersions (services/kafka/nodes.go:50) returns a flat []*MSKVersion{Version, Status} instead -- neither field name ("version"/"status") nor the shape (flat list vs grouped) matches. Every real client's compatibleKafkaVersions decodes as an empty list regardless of what the backend computed: MSKVersion has no sourceVersion or targetVersions member for the deserializer to match.

NOT a tag rename: fixing this means changing GetCompatibleKafkaVersions to return a single-element (or per-current-version) list grouping current cluster version -> its list of compatible upgrade targets, a shape change to the backend method's return type and every caller, not a json-tag edit. Filing per the zquj sweep's tags/keys-only scope rather than half-fixing.

Verify with a real-SDK-client GetCompatibleKafkaVersions call asserting CompatibleKafkaVersions[0].SourceVersion and TargetVersions decode non-nil/non-empty.
close_reason: Closed

title: verifiedpermissions PolicyTemplate is missing Name end-to-end -- structural, not a tag fix
description:
Real AWS PolicyTemplate carries a Name (PolicyTemplateName) member: CreatePolicyTemplateInput.Name and UpdatePolicyTemplateInput.Name are settable (api_op_CreatePolicyTemplate.go:94, api_op_UpdatePolicyTemplate.go:104, verifiedpermissions@v1.36.4), and GetPolicyTemplateOutput / ListPolicyTemplates' PolicyTemplateItem both require a 'name' key (deserializers.go awsAwsjson10_deserializeDocumentPolicyTemplateItem case 'name' -> sv.Name). gopherstack's PolicyTemplate model (services/verifiedpermissions/models.go:84-91) has no Name field at all: createPolicyTemplateInput/updatePolicyTemplateInput never parse it, the backend never stores it, and getPolicyTemplateOutput/policyTemplateView never emit it. Every real client's Name comes back empty on every op.

Found via cmd/keycheck's gopherstack-zquj sweep: it surfaced only as an incidental MISMATCH on ListPolicyTemplates (policyTemplateView writes 'statement', which real PolicyTemplateItem does not have -- that part IS harmless, blind spot #3 shape) -- but chasing that mismatch is what surfaced the real gap, that 'name' is required and never written by Get or List.

NOT a tag rename: fixing this needs a new field threaded through Backend.CreatePolicyTemplate/UpdatePolicyTemplate (interface signature change), the PolicyTemplate model struct, and both output shapes -- real structural work, not the tags/keys-only scope of the zquj sweep. Filing per that constraint rather than half-fixing.

Verify with a real-SDK-client round trip: CreatePolicyTemplate with Name set, then GetPolicyTemplate and ListPolicyTemplates and assert Name round-trips.
close_reason: Closed

title: keycheck: sqs dispatch resolution silently picks legacy XML handler over the real JSON one
description:
cmd/keycheck's ps.opToHandler case-dispatch scan (recordCaseDispatch/findHandlerCall) has no concept of 'two handler functions bound to the same op name conflict' -- it just does ps.opToHandler[op] = handler, last-write-wins by AST file-processing order (alphabetical by filename).

sqs hosts BOTH a modern 'handle<Op>' JSON handler (services/sqs/handler_messages.go etc, what the pinned aws-sdk-go-v2 client actually talks to -- confirmed JSON-RPC 1.0 in services/_PROTOCOLS.md) AND a legacy 'query<Op>' XML/Query-protocol handler (services/sqs/query_messages.go etc) for the SAME op string, left over from before SQS's protocol switch. query_messages.go sorts after handler_messages.go alphabetically, so its case clause overwrites the JSON binding, and keycheck resolves e.g. DeleteMessageBatch to queryDeleteMessageBatch (which marshals XML via marshalXML/XMLDeleteMessageBatchResultEntry) instead of handleDeleteMessageBatch (which correctly builds jsonBatchResult{jsonBatchSuccess{ID string `json:"Id"`}}, already correct).

Running gopherstack-v4a4's struct-tag scan against sqs produced 85 MISMATCH findings across ~13 ops, all traced by hand to this cause -- comparing the wrong (XML-tagged or untagged) handler's fields against the JSON SDK's key set is a meaningless comparison, not a real bug. None of sqs's MISMATCH output should be trusted until this is fixed or worked around.

Fix would need same-op multi-handler detection in ps.opToHandler (e.g. flag when a case clause tries to rebind an op already bound, or prefer handle/json-prefixed handlers over query-prefixed ones) with a test proving it against this exact sqs fixture. Out of scope for gopherstack-v4a4 (documented as KNOWN BLIND SPOT #6 in cmd/keycheck/main.go instead, not fixed).
close_reason: Closed

title: glue: BatchGetTableOptimizer needs a wrapper/nested-TableOptimizer split, not just tag fixes
description:
gopherstack-v4a4 fixed TableOptimizer.Type/.Configuration/.LastRun and TableOptimizerConfiguration.Enabled/.RoleARN struct-tag casing (PascalCase -> lowerCamelCase, matching awsAwsjson11_deserializeDocumentTableOptimizer/TableOptimizerConfiguration in glue@v1.152.0 deserializers.go). That fix is complete and correct for GetTableOptimizer, whose real shape (GetTableOptimizerOutput) nests TableOptimizer directly under the op output with sibling top-level CatalogId/DatabaseName/TableName.

BatchGetTableOptimizer's real per-entry shape is different: awsAwsjson11_deserializeDocumentBatchTableOptimizer switches on catalogId/databaseName/tableName/tableOptimizer (all lowerCamelCase), where tableOptimizer is itself a NESTED sub-object wrapping the same TableOptimizer document one level deeper than GetTableOptimizer's shape.

gopherstack's batchGetTableOptimizerOutput.TableOptimizers []*TableOptimizer (services/glue/handler_table_optimizers.go) reuses the SAME flat TableOptimizer struct (services/glue/models.go) for both ops, so for BatchGetTableOptimizer, Type/Configuration/LastRun end up as siblings of CatalogID/DatabaseName/TableName instead of nested under a tableOptimizer key. Casing alone cannot fix this -- it needs a real restructure: a new wrapper type (BatchTableOptimizer-shaped: catalogId/databaseName/tableName/tableOptimizer) with the existing TableOptimizer nested inside it, used only by BatchGetTableOptimizer, leaving GetTableOptimizer's shape untouched.

Also: GetTableOptimizerOutput's nested TableOptimizer.CatalogID/DatabaseName/TableName fields are fabricated duplicates -- the real inner TableOptimizer document has no such members at all (confirmed via its deserializer's case list: only configuration/configurationSource/lastRun/type). GetTableOptimizerOutput's real CatalogId/DatabaseName/TableName live one level up on getTableOptimizerOutput itself (already correct). Once BatchGetTableOptimizer gets its own wrapper type, consider whether TableOptimizer.CatalogID/DatabaseName/TableName can be dropped entirely from the shared TableOptimizer struct.

Out of scope for gopherstack-v4a4 (tag-only campaign, restructuring explicitly forbidden). See services/glue/PARITY.md, '2026-08-22 gopherstack-v4a4' section, for full detail and SDK file:line citations.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] response struct TAGS are unchecked against the deserializer, the same way map keys were
notes:
Found 2026-08-22. glue QuerySchemaVersionMetadata tagged its field
json:"MetadataInfo" where the real deserializer switches on MetadataInfoMap,
so the entire metadata map -- the only thing that op returns -- was dropped by
every real client. Fixed in c3aa73e59.

THE POINT IS THE SURFACE, NOT THE ONE BUG. cmd/keycheck (gopherstack-zquj)
checks hand-written map[string]any keys against the pinned SDK's deserializer
case lists. Response STRUCT TAGS are the other half of the same wire surface
and have never been swept that way. A wrong tag fails identically and
invisibly: an exact-match awsjson deserializer drops the unknown key with no
error.

WHY THE EXISTING TESTS CANNOT FIND IT, which is the whole reason this needs a
mechanical pass. Two glue tests decode the response through their OWN local
struct tagged json:"MetadataInfo". They passed before the fix and pass after.
A raw-body test asserts the key its author typed, which is the same key the
handler author typed. Nine such tests asserted wrong keys as correct during
the gopherstack-6flj sweep.

METHOD, and it must not be grep: seven grep-derived scopes this campaign were
wrong, one 11x low, one 100 percent false positives, one of mine inflated by
counting test files. Extend cmd/keycheck, or build alongside it: for each op,
resolve the real wire key set from awsAwsjson1x_deserializeOpDocument<Op>Output
and its nested deserializeDocument<Type> case lists, then compare against the
json tags on the structs the handler actually marshals. keycheck already does
the SDK half; only the handler half differs.

BEWARE, all four learned the hard way this session:
  - Casing is NOT uniform within one nested tree. scheduler's real API uses
    awsvpcConfiguration and capacityProvider alongside Subnets, SecurityGroups
    and AssignPublicIp. A blanket rule would have broken three fields.
  - A dynamic map<string,T> field has no switch in the deserializer at all, so
    an empty allowed-key set means "dynamic", not "nothing is legal". This is
    keycheck blind spot #4 and it produced most of 82 false positives.
  - Unreadable must never be reported as clean. That is why keycheck exits
    non-zero on an ERROR row, after cmd/opcensus spent weeks reporting silent
    zeros for services with 152 and 119 ops (gopherstack-jq8x).
  - Do NOT convert map literals to tagged structs or vice versa. Each
    construction has its own exposure; this issue is about checking tags, not
    restructuring.

PROOF STANDARD: a real-SDK-client round trip asserting the member decodes
non-nil. A raw-body assertion is worthless here by construction. Confirm each
test fails against the unfixed tag.

SIZING: unknown and deliberately not guessed. glue is one confirmed instance.

FIRST TASK, small and owed: add the real-client assertion for glue
QuerySchemaVersionMetadata that c3aa73e59 could not carry.

Related: gopherstack-zquj, gopherstack-6flj, gopherstack-0kk8.

2026-08-22 continuation pass. FIRST TASK from prior notes was already done (glue's
QuerySchemaVersionMetadata real-client test exists,
handler_query_schema_version_metadata_realclient_test.go). Re-ran the extended
keycheck struct-tag scan fresh (fresh binary, current HEAD) across all 138
reachable json-protocol services (141 total minus ssm/cloudwatchlogs/kinesis,
another agent's territory this session): 39 clean, 70 mismatch, 21 partial, 8
unresolved -- close to the prior pass's 39/66/16/17 (this session's ~208 commits
of drift plus a slightly different counting method account for the difference).

SCOPE: of the 141 json-protocol services, 67 (48%) define at least one locally
Output-tagged struct (this issue's exposure) summing to ~4085 keycheck-resolved
ops; the other ~74 build responses purely from map[string]any literals
(gopherstack-zquj's domain, already fully swept) or neither pattern. Method:
regex census of  per service dir, cross-
referenced against keycheck's own per-service ops-resolved count -- an
approximation (over-counts nested/domain-collision Output types the way
kinesis/iot demonstrate below), not a mechanically-derived exact count.

Triaged every CASE-MISMATCH-shaped finding (the highest-confidence signal --
an exact case mismatch under a case-SENSITIVE protocol can't be a protocol
quirk) across the full sweep: awsconfig (9), iot (18), medialive (225,
already-documented artifact), quicksight (4, already-documented artifact),
dynamodb (2), macie2 (1).

REAL: awsconfig -- 9 fields across 4 ops (DescribeAggregationAuthorizations'
AuthorizedAccountId/AuthorizedAwsRegion, DescribeOrganizationConfigRules'
OrganizationConfigRuleName, DescribeOrganizationConformancePacks'
OrganizationConformancePackName, DescribeDeliveryChannelStatus's whole
DeliveryChannelStatus/DeliveryChannelStatusInfo). Each confirmed against
configservice@v1.68.4's deserializers.go, fixed, proven with 4 new real-SDK-
client tests in services/awsconfig/wire_field_fixes_test.go, each confirmed
to fail against the pre-fix tag and hand-reverted/restored byte-identical.
PARITY.md updated (front-matter op lines + dated body entry). Two structural
follow-ups filed, not fixed: gopherstack-ru0y (DeliveryChannelStatus missing
ConfigSnapshotDeliveryInfo + wrong shared nested type), gopherstack-xit0
(OrganizationConfigRule missing required Arn).

ARTIFACT (three new instances of already-documented blind-spot classes, no
code changed): iot's 18 -- OUTPUT-SUFFIX NAME COLLISION (same class as
kinesis): types.go's untagged domain CreatePolicyOutput/etc (backend return
type, never marshaled) collides with the *Output-suffix heuristic; the
actual handler already re-keys through correct lowerCamelCase key consts.
dynamodb's 2 -- an S3 *manifest file* (import_export_s3.go, internal
export bookkeeping, never the HTTP response) pulled into the same-package
call-graph walk. macie2's 1 -- an enum VALUE ("UNKNOWN"/"unknown"),
not a JSON key, misclassified by the scanner.

STILL UNVERIFIED from the prior pass's list, minus what this pass covered:
roughly 88 services (70 mismatch + 21 partial - awsconfig - the three
artifact-confirmed - medialive/quicksight/kinesis already known) remain
hand-unverified. Per-service raw keycheck output from both this pass and the
prior one is preserved under this session's scratchpad v4a4-2/ and v4a4-3/
(raw_<svc>.txt / raw/<svc>.txt) for the next pass -- most NotInTree-only
findings (no CASE-MISMATCH) are lower-confidence per blind spots #2/#4 and
were not prioritized this pass given the CASE-MISMATCH signal's much higher
hit rate (1 real cluster / 6 checked vs the documented near-0% base rate for
NotInTree-only findings).
STATE, 2026-08-23. The tooling half of this issue is DONE and was already done before today: cmd/keycheck (3117 lines) checks response struct json tags against the pinned deserializer case lists, alongside the map-key check from gopherstack-zquj. Verified directly -- I briefed a worker to build it and it correctly reported the tool already existed. Remaining work is TRIAGE of the sweep output, not tooling.

MEASURED YIELD, reported honestly rather than flatteringly. The high-confidence CASE-MISMATCH bucket was fully triaged in earlier sessions. This session sampled the REMAINING bucket -- findings with no case-mismatch signal -- across nine services: scheduler, identitystore, kms, efs, transcribe, mq, vpclattice, dms, kafka.

  8 of 9 services false positive; 1 real (dms)
  13 of ~40 raw instances real, and all 13 trace to ONE root cause

So the instance-level number (33%) flatters it; the real rate is one bug in nine services sampled. That matches the near-zero base rate this campaign has measured for every non-case-mismatch mechanical finding.

The three false-positive causes are all previously documented blind spots, which is itself a useful result -- the noise is structural, not random:
  - shared error-envelope helpers polluting a service's key set (identitystore ResourceType, efs ErrorCode/Message)
  - the walker following into unrelated sibling-op code (kms PrivateKeyPlaintext, Plaintext, PrimaryRegion)
  - harmless EXTRA fields that real AWS's Create response genuinely omits (scheduler Description/ScheduleExpression, mq engineType/engineVersion, vpclattice createdAt/lastUpdatedAt)

The third category is worth noting: extra fields are not wire bugs. A real client ignores them. Only a MISSING or MISNAMED key drops data.

CONCLUSION FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: the case-mismatch bucket is the productive one and it is exhausted. The no-signal bucket is running at roughly the same near-zero rate as the four dead classes in gopherstack-n3zi. Do not spend another full pass on it without a new discriminator.
close_reason: Verified 2026-08-28. cmd/keycheck now also checks json struct tags on response structs, and the sweep concluded the case-mismatch bucket is exhausted.

title: [bug] sagemaker Batch{Add,Delete,Reboot,Replace}ClusterNodes never write Failed/Successful, drop values on every real client
description:
Found by cmd/keycheck's awsjson sweep (gopherstack-zquj), same class as wafv2's
CheckCapacity bug (b97408b98). handler_cluster.go's shared
batchClusterNodesWithFailures helper writes an invented top-level "ClusterArn"
plus a flat []string under "Failures" ("Errors" for Delete), and never writes
"Successful" at all, for all four of BatchAddClusterNodes,
BatchDeleteClusterNodes, BatchRebootClusterNodes, BatchReplaceClusterNodes.

The real outputs (api_op_Batch{Add,Delete,Reboot,Replace}ClusterNodes.go,
aws-sdk-go-v2/service/sagemaker@v1.263.2) all require:
  - Failed: a list of PER-OP-TYPED error structs, not a flat string list --
    types.BatchAddClusterNodesError keys by InstanceGroupName+FailedCount;
    the other three key by node/instance ID with their own distinct types
    (BatchDeleteClusterNodesError, BatchRebootClusterNodesError,
    BatchReplaceClusterNodesError).
  - Successful: []string for Delete/Reboot/Replace, but
    []types.NodeAdditionResult for Add.

Net effect: a real client calling any of these four ops always decodes
Failed == nil and Successful == nil, regardless of what actually happened.

NOT fixed in the zquj sweep pass: this needs per-op-typed error structs (not a
key rename) and, for BatchAddClusterNodes specifically, a backend signature
change since InMemoryBackend.BatchAddClusterNodes currently returns only a
flat failures list, never which nodes succeeded. Out of scope for a
"fix keys only, don't restructure" pass -- building the four distinct Failed
item shapes is itself a struct introduction.

See services/sagemaker/PARITY.md's 2026-08-22 dated Notes entry for full
detail and SDK file:line citations.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] required request members three create ops never validate
notes:
Found 2026-08-22 incidentally, by the gopherstack-4ly2 second sweep. That
sweep looked for the OPPOSITE class (handlers demanding members AWS does not
require) and found none, but kept tripping over the mirror on the way.

This is the under-validation class, not the over-validation one. Related to
gopherstack-7rq1 (CLOSED, and a different shape -- that one covered request
fields present in the model but absent from the wire struct).

CONFIRMED against the pinned SDK:

  eks AssociateIdentityProviderConfig -- OidcIdentityProviderConfigRequest
    marks THREE members required: ClientId, IdentityProviderConfigName and
    IssuerUrl. gopherstack decodes IdentityProviderConfigName with an
    omitempty tag and validates none of the three. Verified directly:
    types.go's required markers versus handler_identity_providers.go:73.

REPORTED BY THE SWEEP, NOT YET VERIFIED BY ME -- confirm each before fixing:
  organizations InviteAccountToOrganization and
    InviteOrganizationToTransferResponsibility -- Target.Type unvalidated.
  glue CreateDataCellsFilter -- DatabaseName, TableCatalogId and TableName
    unvalidated.

WHY THIS KEEPS RECURRING. sagemaker's parity-25 pass found nine required
members decoded and never validated in a single file tier, and glue's
GetEntityRecords was found demanding an optional filter while never enforcing
the required Limit. That last shape matters: an op can be wrong in BOTH
directions at once, and each half makes the other look handled. A sweep for
missing validation sees a check on the op and moves on; a sweep for
over-validation sees a required-looking check and moves on.

METHOD: read each op's own SDK required set against its own handler, in both

title: [bug] the operations badge counts PARITY.md entries, not operations, so every coverage ratio built on it is wrong
notes:
Found 2026-08-22 while re-measuring gopherstack-n3zi.

cmd/gendocs/badges.go:88 totalOperations sums len(doc.Ops) across manifests --
that is the count of ops: ENTRIES in PARITY.md, and entries are hand-grouped
families. One entry can name five real operations. The badge currently reads
6332.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY: lightsail's GetSupportedOperations returns 161 operations.
s3's returns 55. The badge's per-service contribution is the manifest entry
count, not these.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A COSMETIC NUMBER. gopherstack-n3zi's headline -- "77
percent of operations are never touched by a real SDK client" -- used the
badge as its denominator. Re-measuring against GetSupportedOperations, the
n3zi pass put the real total near 10,784 and typed-client coverage at 17
percent invoked / 11 percent decoded. I did not independently confirm 10,784
and it should be re-derived before being quoted, but the DIRECTION is
established from source: the badge undercounts, so every ratio built on it
overstates coverage.

Note the badge understates the emulator's breadth, so fixing it makes the
project look better, not worse. The problem is that it is not a denominator.

WHAT TO DECIDE, not just fix:
  1. Should the badge count real dispatched operations (sum of every service's
     GetSupportedOperations) instead of manifest entries? That is the honest
     number and cmd/opcensus already computes it.
  2. If the grouped-entry count is deliberate -- families are the unit humans
     audit -- then RENAME the badge so it does not claim to count operations,
     and publish the real op count separately.
Do not silently swap the number: the README, the manifests and several bd
issues all quote 6332-era figures, and changing the badge without reconciling
them replaces one wrong denominator with two.

CAVEAT ON opcensus: the n3zi pass found it resolves 0 ops for ssm and
route53resolver because their dispatch tables route through more helper hops
than its chase depth handles (hand-counted 152 and 72). qldb and qldbsession
are genuinely 0, being unimplemented placeholders. See gopherstack-jq8x, which
already records opcensus reporting a silent zero for ssm and route53resolver.
Fix that before trusting a repo-wide total.

Related: gopherstack-n3zi, gopherstack-jq8x.
RECOMMENDATION FROM THE jq8x PASS (2026-08-22), for a human to decide: RENAME the badge, do NOT swap the number. Reason: len(doc.Ops) drives the badge total AND the per-service Operations column in readmetable.go:64-65, which renders ~160 times across generated READMEs. Swapping to real dispatched-op counts silently changes the meaning of that column everywhere, which is a docs-wide change, not a badge edit. The grouped-entry count also has genuine audit value -- families are the unit the parity audit actually reviews and grades -- so replacing it loses information rather than correcting it. Proposed: relabel 'AWS operations' as 'op families' or 'PARITY entries', keep the entry count under that label, and publish the real dispatched-op total as a separate explicitly-labelled figure. RECONCILIATION SCOPE, checked by grep: only .badges/operations.svg contains the literal 6332; no other file or bd issue quotes the digit. But the LABEL 'AWS operations' appears at README.md:19 and implicitly via the readmetable Operations column, so both need the same rename. TRUSTWORTHY TOTAL NOW AVAILABLE: cmd/opcensus is fixed (gopherstack-jq8x, commit 8b6af439c) and reports 10,565 operations across 160 real services with zero unresolved rows. Caveat: comprehend is ~4 high (89 vs a verified 85) because it builds op names by runtime string concatenation that no AST walker can recover. Note this does NOT reconcile with n3zi's unconfirmed 10,784 -- that gap is unexplained and should be resolved before either number is published.
## Fixed 2026-08-22 by relabel, not by reassignment

Both numbers reproduced independently before touching anything:
  displayed 6,389 / real 10,565 across 160 services / undercount 4,176 (~40%).

Two separate defects, and the second is the structural one:
  - len(doc.Ops) counts ops: ENTRIES, a hand-grouped audit unit -- one entry
    can name several operations (AddPermission/RemovePermission is one row).
  - the sum never consulted doc.Families, so ten family-audited services
    contributed ZERO. ec2 has a families: block and no ops: block, so its 785
    operations counted as none. Those ten hold 1,608 operations between them.

Every rendering now says PARITY entries: badge, summary table header, the
intro prose that claimed 'API operations audited', and the per-service README
row. 152 files regenerated.

DELIBERATELY NOT SWAPPING IN THE REAL NUMBER. Doing so would silently
redefine the Operations column across ~160 generated READMEs, and sourcing the
honest figure needs opcensus's ~800-line AST census extracted from package
main with its 524-line test suite migrated. That is an architectural change,
not a badge fix, and this issue's own note flagged the swap as a decision for
a human. Filed separately.

Drift runs both ways: ten services record MORE entries than they have ops
(forecast 21 v 8, fis 37 v 26, amplify 48 v 37). Spot-checking forecast showed
the fault is on the opcensus side -- it builds its op list from a runtime map
the AST walk does not chase -- so that is recorded against gopherstack-jq8x,
not against the manifests.

title: [security] CodeQL flags the ssm document Sha1/Sha256 parity hashes as weak sensitive-data hashing
notes:
Found 2026-08-22 by reading PR #2433's CodeQL check, which FAILS with
"2 new alerts including 2 high severity security vulnerabilities".

WHAT IT FLAGS. rule go/weak-sensitive-data-hashing, high, two instances at
services/ssm/documents.go:25 and :26 -- sha256.Sum256 and sha1.Sum inside
documentHashes(content string).

THESE ARE GENUINELY NEW ON THIS BRANCH. documentHashes does not exist at the
merge-base with main; this branch added it. CodeQL's "alerts not introduced by
this pull request might have been detected because the code changes were too
large" caveat does NOT explain these two. Verified with
git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)..HEAD.

WHY THE CODE IS CORRECT AS WRITTEN. DocumentDescription declares Hash,
HashType and a separate deprecated Sha1 member. Real AWS computes Hash as the
SHA256 of the document content and populates Sha1 for backward compatibility
(ssm@v1.73.4 types/enums.go:708-724, DocumentHashType Sha256|Sha1). An
emulator cannot return AWS's Sha1 field without computing SHA1. Removing it
would reintroduce a missing-required-member bug of exactly the kind this
campaign has been fixing.

WHY CODEQL STILL HAS A POINT, AND WHY I AM NOT SILENTLY SUPPRESSING IT. The
taint source is real: SSM document content can legitimately contain
parameters named password or secret, and this hashes whatever content it is
given. The rule's specific claim -- that this is password hashing needing a
computationally expensive function -- is wrong, because the value is a
content-integrity checksum echoed back on the wire, never an authentication
credential and never compared against a stored credential. But "we hash
user-supplied content that may contain secrets with SHA1" is an accurate
description of the code, and that judgement belongs to a human, not to me.

The existing //nolint:gosec comments already state this reasoning. They do not
silence CodeQL, which is a separate analyser.

OPTIONS, none of which I have taken:
  1. Dismiss both alerts in the GitHub Security tab as "used in tests" /
     "false positive" with the parity justification. Requires repo admin.
     Leaves the code unchanged and unblocks the check.
  2. Add a CodeQL suppression comment or a query filter in the workflow.
     Narrower than a dismissal but puts the exception in the repo.
  3. Change the code -- NOT recommended. Any change that stops computing
     SHA1 breaks DocumentDescription parity.

BLOCKING IMPACT: the CodeQL check on PR #2433 is red because of these two.
Everything else on that run is green.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] wire-shape fixes that changed a persisted model without bumping its snapshot version
notes:
Found 2026-08-21 as a follow-up to gopherstack-tp8x item 1, fixed in
4c9c14d46. Filed because the eks case is unlikely to be the only one.

THE SHAPE. A parity fix changes a model that is also persisted -- renames a
field, merges two, deletes a type -- and does not bump that service's
snapshot version constant.

    9e4104c54 merged ElasticLoadBalancing into KubernetesNetworkConfig and
    deleted the NetworkingConfig type. Cluster's persisted shape changed.
    eksSnapshotVersion stayed at 1.

THE FAILURE IS SILENT, WHICH IS WHY IT NEEDS A SWEEP. A pre-fix snapshot does
not fail to load against the new shape. It decodes cleanly and drops whatever
was stored under the field that no longer exists. The version guard exists to
discard a snapshot it cannot faithfully read, and it cannot fire while the
version still claims the shape is unchanged. Nothing errors; data is just
gone.

THE RULE: a wire-shape fix that touches a persisted model is not finished
until the snapshot version moves with it.

WHY THIS IS PROBABLY REPO-WIDE. This session alone landed roughly 30 parity
fixes that changed model structs, across sagemaker, kafka, firehose,
autoscaling, cloudtrail, wafv2, codepipeline, rekognition, textract, emr,
timestreamquery and guardduty. The wrapper-key campaign before it landed
50-plus more. Each was reviewed for wire correctness. NONE was reviewed for
persistence impact -- the question was never asked until now.

METHOD. Do not grep for renamed fields; five grep-derived scopes this campaign
were wrong. Instead:
  1. list every service with a snapshot version constant and a registered
     table set;
  2. for each, diff its persisted model structs across this branch's history
     (git log -p on the model file, or diff against the merge-base with main);
  3. flag any commit that changed a persisted struct's fields without touching
     the version constant in the same commit.
Step 3 is mechanical and checkable, which is what makes this tractable.

pkgs/persistence has a snapshot-version guard and a test
(snapshotversion_guard_test.go) whose scanner was broadened this session to
find every *Snapshot-suffixed struct. CHECK WHETHER THAT GUARD CAN BE
EXTENDED to fail when a registered struct's field set changes without a
version bump -- a test that catches this class automatically is worth far more
than one audit of it.

BEWARE: bumping a version discards user snapshots on upgrade. That is correct
when the shape genuinely changed and destructive when it did not. Do not bump
defensively. Confirm the field set actually changed before moving a version.

Related: gopherstack-tp8x, gopherstack-r80d, gopherstack-6flj.
FIRST PASS DONE 2026-08-21. Guard extended and VERIFIED to fail on the original eks bug (orchestrator re-verified independently: removed the field, TestSnapshotVersionGuard failed, restored byte-identical). Root cause of the original miss: the guard only saw *Snapshot-suffixed structs one level deep, while ~150 of 168 services persist via store.Register + Tables map[string]json.RawMessage, erasing the domain type. 15 services found with unbumped shape changes; 3 fixed (sagemaker 1->2, bedrockagent 2->3, ecr 1->2). 2 examined and correctly NOT bumped: ssm (field never existed on real AWS, synthetic seed only, no user data) and inspector2 (bump would be INERT -- OrgConfig is a direct backendSnapshot field, so the outer decode fails before the version check is reached; failure is already loud, different class). 10 REMAIN, all confirmed to route through Tables so a bump would be effective: appsync, mediaconvert, omics, macie2, bedrock, athena, cloudwatchlogs, codecommit, firehose, pipes. Each needs individual confirmation before its constant moves -- a wrong bump discards user snapshots.

title: [bug] hand-written map[string]any response keys are unchecked by any compiler or scan
notes:
Found 2026-08-21 by gopherstack-r80d batch 30, as the flip side of a clean
result. ssoadmin, mediatailor and shield returned zero required-output bugs
BECAUSE they build responses as map[string]any literals rather than tagged
structs -- there are no omitempty tags to get wrong, and every required key is
written unconditionally.

THE COST OF THAT IMMUNITY. shield holds 277 map[string]any literals; ssoadmin
holds 622. Each one is a hand-written key string. Nothing checks them:

  - the Go compiler cannot -- a map key is just a string;
  - the required-output scan cannot -- it reads struct tags;
  - a raw-body test cannot -- it asserts the key the author expected, which is
    the same key the author typed. Nine such tests asserted wrong keys as
    correct during the wrapper-key sweep.

So a typo'd or wrongly-cased key in these services is silently dropped by the
real client and invisible to every instrument this repo has. That is exactly
the gopherstack-6flj wrapper-key class, in the one construction where no
existing tool can find it.

SIZING: unknown, and deliberately not guessed. 899 literals across two
services is the count of SITES, not of bugs. Most are presumably correct.

METHOD, and it must not be grep: five grep-derived scopes in this campaign
were wrong, one by 11x and one 100% false positives. The tractable approach is
a type-checked pass -- for each op, resolve the real output type's JSON member
names from the SDK deserializer's case list, then compare against the string
keys the handler actually writes. cmd/opcensus and the sweep's deserializer
reading are the precedent.

THE STRUCTURAL FIX is already recorded as gopherstack-0shs: swf derives its
keys rather than hand-writing them. Deriving keys in these services would end
the class rather than audit it, and is worth costing before a 899-site audit
is attempted.

DO NOT convert these to tagged structs as a first move. That trades a
no-compiler-check exposure for the omitempty exposure this campaign has found
30-plus bugs in. Whatever is done should be verified by real-SDK-client round
trips either way.

Related: gopherstack-r80d, gopherstack-6flj, gopherstack-0shs.

title: [bug] over-validation whose fix is a feature: backend cannot serve the documented alternate identifier
notes:
Split out of gopherstack-4ly2's first sweep (2026-08-21). 4ly2 covers
over-validation that is safe to DELETE. This issue covers the harder half:
the same class where deleting the check would turn a 400 into a WRONG ANSWER,
because the backend has no way to serve the documented alternate path.

wafv2 GetWebACL/GetRuleGroup were of this kind and were fixed in b78281101 by
adding ARN lookups over existing secondary indexes -- cheap because the index
already existed. The seven below are not cheap.

CONFIRMED INSTANCES, each verified against the pinned SDK doc text:

  batch ListJobs.jobQueue -- real alternates ArrayJobId/MultiNodeJobId do not
    exist as fields on gopherstack's request struct at all. The handler's own
    comment ("AWS Batch ListJobs requires a grouping key") is factually wrong
    about real AWS. Left unedited on purpose: correcting the comment without
    the feature would make the code read as done when it is not.
  transfer CreateConnector.Url -- conditional on non-VPC-Lattice egress.
    gopherstack has no EgressConfig or VPC-Lattice connector support.
  rekognition SearchUsers.UserId -- doc allows FaceId instead; backend method
    takes no FaceId.
  cloudtrail DescribeQuery.QueryId -- doc allows QueryAlias; no alias lookup.
  glue GetEntityRecords, ListEntities.ConnectionName -- backend indexes
    entities solely by connection name.
  textract ListAdapterVersions.AdapterId -- backend needs an existing adapter
    to enumerate versions; no cross-adapter index.
  codepipeline ListDeployActionExecutionTargets.pipelineName -- no global
    execution-ID index. Note ActionExecutionId, the field actually required,
    IS validated and then discarded (`_ = executionID`), a pre-existing stub.

THE RULE THIS ESTABLISHES: an over-validation is safe to delete only when the
backend can already serve the alternate path. Otherwise the check is the only
thing preventing a confidently wrong response, and deleting it converts a
false negative into a false positive -- strictly worse, because a 400 is
visible and a wrong 200 is not.

SEQUENCING: each of these is an independent feature (a secondary index, or a
request field plus its lookup). Do them one service at a time, and only remove
the validation in the same commit that adds the path.

DO NOT confuse with the 13 candidates 4ly2 examined and left because the
validation is LEGITIMATE -- sole identifier with sibling ops marking the same
field required, an SDK modeling gap rather than true optionality. Those are
recorded in 4ly2's notes and should stay as they are.

Related: gopherstack-4ly2.
FIVE OF SEVEN DONE as of 2026-08-22: codepipeline (efc4e937f), rekognition (8eabbbbad), cloudtrail (a2b12380d), textract (0e9eb742f), glue (this commit). REMAINING TWO: batch ListJobs (needs ArrayJobId/MultiNodeJobId request fields that do not exist plus array/multi-node job modelling) and transfer CreateConnector (needs EgressConfig/VPC-Lattice support that does not exist). Both are genuine features, not deletions. SIZING RELIABILITY: my own estimates in this issue were wrong three times out of five -- cloudtrail understated (said a field did not exist; it did, declared but never populated), textract and glue both OVERSTATED (claimed new indexes/features were needed when the backing state already existed). Treat any remaining estimate as a hypothesis to test, not a budget. NEW PATTERN, seen in codepipeline and now glue: an op can be wrong in BOTH directions at once -- demanding an optional filter while never enforcing a genuinely required member. Single-direction sweeps miss it because each half looks like the other is handled.

title: [bug] handlers that reject requests real AWS accepts, by requiring members the input does not mark required
notes:
New class, found 2026-08-21 in sagemaker's CreateModel and fixed in
d2f30feb6. It is the MIRROR of everything this campaign has swept for.

THE SHAPE. A handler validates a member as required when the real input does
not mark it so, and returns 400 for a request real AWS accepts.

    CreateModelInput marks exactly ONE member required: ModelName.
    gopherstack rejected any request without ExecutionRoleArn.

So a client doing something legitimate got a validation error from the
emulator and a success from AWS. Every prior finding in this campaign is a
false positive -- the emulator accepting or emitting something wrong. This is
a false NEGATIVE, and no sweep so far could see it: they all ask whether
required members are read, never whether non-required ones are demanded.

WHY IT SURVIVES. TestCreateModel_RequiresExecutionRoleArn asserted the
rejection directly. Not a fixture gap, not a missing assertion -- a test
written to pin behaviour AWS does not have. A suite built from the
implementation cannot fail on the implementation being wrong, and here it
actively defended it.

Note the opposite defect sat in the same file tier: CreateAlgorithm never
validated TrainingSpecification, which IS required. Same pass, same service,
opposite directions. A service is not internally consistent about this, so
per-op reading is the only method that works.

THE CHECK, per op: read the real input type's required set, then read the
handler's validation. Anything the handler demands that the SDK does not mark
required is a candidate. Then confirm the demand actually rejects -- some
handlers read a field defensively without erroring, which is fine.

BEWARE THE OPPOSITE ERROR. Some validation is legitimate even when the SDK
does not mark the member required:
  - the SDK's own CLIENT-SIDE validator may reject it before the wire, in
    which case the emulator agreeing is harmless (though also pointless);
  - a member may be conditionally required -- required only alongside another
    field -- which the required marker cannot express;
  - gopherstack may deliberately be stricter, and several such cases are
    already recorded as deliberate in PARITY.md gaps.
Read the doc text and the validator before removing a check. Removing a
legitimate one turns a false negative into a false positive.

SIZING: unknown. No sweep has looked. sagemaker's CreateModel is the only
confirmed instance. Do not assume it is rare -- nobody has counted -- and do
not assume it is common either.

METHOD: do not grep. Four grep-derived scopes this campaign were wrong -- one
100% false positives, one 11x low, one that missed an entire token class, one
that counted 12 when the real figure was 90. Compare each op's SDK-required
set against the handler's validation with a type-checked pass, then read the
write path.

PROOF STANDARD: a real-SDK-client call omitting the over-demanded member,
asserting it SUCCEEDS. The inverse of this campaign's usual test.

Related: gopherstack-oc9v (found it).
FIRST SWEEP DONE 2026-08-21, commits d4f24bc88 + b78281101. Sized the class: 1434 raw AST hits across 76 services, cross-referenced against real SDK required sets, yielding 29 genuine top-level candidates, ALL hand-triaged. 5 fixed (lakeformation x2, timestreamwrite x1, wafv2 x2). 7 left as gopherstack-<pending> -- backend cannot serve the alternate path, fix is a feature not a deletion. 13 left because the validation is LEGITIMATE: sole identifier, no alternate on the struct, and sibling ops in the same service mark the identical field required (codebuild x4, codedeploy x5, glue x2, support, xray) -- an SDK modeling gap, not true optionality. 1 already-disclosed structural gap (directoryservice, gopherstack-10hx). 2 tool false positives (xray compound-OR conditions, already correct). NOT REACHED: ~51 dotted/nested-path candidates needing per-op nested-struct resolution, and a 53-entry bucket dominated by case-mismatched op names (handleCreateHTTPNamespace vs SDK CreateHttpNamespace) -- an undercount, not hidden bugs; 2 spot-checks there came back correctly-required. The overdemand scratch tool was NOT promoted to cmd/: compound-condition false positives and case-sensitive op matching must be fixed before it can be trusted for a blind sweep.
SECOND SWEEP DONE 2026-08-22: both unreached buckets closed at ZERO new bugs. Bucket 1 (nested/dotted-path): ~20 genuine reject-style checks hand-audited across timestreamquery, rekognition, ce, acm, sagemaker, identitystore, eks, lambda, organizations, lakeformation, dynamodb, s3, datasync, glue, route53resolver, efs, kinesis, fsx -- all matched the SDK's real nested requiredness, or were single-arm unions, conditional requirements, or the already-closed directoryservice gap (gopherstack-10hx). Bucket 2 (case-mismatched op names): a rebuilt case-insensitive resolver found 140 handler-to-op resolutions repo-wide that fail exact match; 26 of those contain an actual validation demand; all 26 hand-verified correct. So bucket 2 was an undercount, as the first sweep suspected, and NOT hidden bugs. ONE CANDIDATE CONSIDERED FOR 2wvq AND REJECTED: route53resolver DisassociateResolverEndpointIpAddress demands IpAddress.IpId, which the shared IpAddressUpdate type does not mark required -- but the sibling UpdateResolverEndpoint's UpdateIpAddress.IpId IS required, the same modelling-gap pattern that disqualified 13 candidates in the first sweep, and the backend has no non-ipID lookup path anyway. TOOL VERDICT: do not promote to cmd/. Union arms, conditional requirements and shared-struct modelling gaps keep the false-positive rate too high without a human reading AWS prose docs, which the SDK's required markers do not capture. The narrow case-insensitive name resolver is worth keeping as a pre-triage scoping utility only. NOTE the class itself is NOT dead -- gopherstack-jodk found a real instance (cognitoidentity SetIdentityPoolRoles) via terraform CI the same day. Static validator reading cannot see which caller depends on the rule; over-validation bites on destroy and clear legs no unit test here exercises.

title: apigateway GetSdk: header-vs-body confusion (JSON-wraps a binary response)
description: Found 2026-08-21 while fixing gopherstack-tp8x's medialive DescribeInputDeviceThumbnail (same bug class). title: [bug] Update handlers that replace a stored structure wholesale, deleting fields the narrower update type cannot carry
notes:
New subclass, found 2026-08-21 in sagemaker's UpdateCodeRepository and fixed
in 1ac934042. Every other bug this campaign has found is accept-and-drop --
a field parsed and ignored, or emitted under a wrong key. THIS ONE DESTROYS
EXISTING STATE.

THE SHAPE. AWS routinely gives Create and Update different types for one
concept, with the Update type NARROWER:

    types.GitConfig          -> RepositoryUrl, Branch, SecretArn   (create)
    types.GitConfigForUpdate -> SecretArn                          (update)

sagemaker's handler stored the Update payload wholesale over the existing
record. A real client can only ever send SecretArn, so every Update silently
deleted RepositoryUrl and Branch from the repository it was updating. The
write succeeded, the response looked correct, and the data was gone.

WHY IT SURVIVES TESTING. TestHandler_UpdateCodeRepository created its fixture
with no GitConfig at all and never inspected the Update's result content.
There was nothing to destroy and nothing checked. The failure needs a test
that creates WITH the wider fields, updates with the narrower payload, and
then asserts the untouched fields SURVIVED -- an assertion almost nobody
writes.

SIZING, rough and deliberately a floor. A quick scan of the pinned SDKs finds
12 *ForUpdate types plus a longer tail of *Update-suffixed ones (batch's
ComputeResourceUpdate, backup's RestoreTestingPlanForUpdate and
RestoreTestingSelectionForUpdate, appstream's AgentAccessConfigForUpdate,
and others). That counts TYPES, not bugs -- most handlers may merge
correctly. It is a starting set.

Note the class is broader than the *ForUpdate naming: any Update op whose
input type has fewer members than the stored structure is a candidate,
however AWS named it. Do not key the search on the suffix alone.

THE CHECK, per candidate. Find where the Update handler writes the decoded
payload into the store. If it assigns or replaces a struct or map rather than
merging field by field, and the update type is narrower than the stored one,
it is this bug. Where the update type is genuinely identical to the create
type, wholesale replacement is correct -- confirm rather than assume.

PROOF STANDARD: create with the wide shape, update with the narrow one,
assert the fields absent from the update type still hold their original
values. A round-trip that only checks the updated field passes over this bug
without touching it.

DO NOT GREP FOR IT. Three grep-derived scopes this campaign were wrong -- one
entirely false positives, one 11x low, one that missed a whole token class.
Compare the Update input type's member set against the stored type's, then
read the handler's write path.

Related: gopherstack-oc9v (found it).
Coverage-gap sweep (2026-08-21), closing the two blind spots this issue's
parent sweep (5536d43de) explicitly named:

1. ~37 Update* methods on receivers other than *InMemoryBackend. Real count,
   derived from `func (.*) Update[A-Z]` across all non-test .go files under
   services/, grouped by receiver: 974 InMemoryBackend, 9 InMemoryDB
   (dynamodb's differently-named backend struct), plus noopBackend(22)/
   stubBackend(3)/mockBackend(1)/mockLambdaStorageBackend(1) -- all of which
   turned out to live ONLY in _test.go files (router-dispatch test doubles,
   not real write paths). So the real non-InMemoryBackend candidate set was
   9, not ~37. All 9 dynamodb InMemoryDB Update* methods read by hand
   against aws-sdk-go-v2/service/dynamodb@v1.63.1: 8 already merge correctly
   (UpdateContinuousBackups/UpdateContributorInsights/UpdateGlobalTable/
   UpdateGlobalTableSettings/UpdateItem/UpdateKinesisStreamingDestination/
   UpdateTable/UpdateTimeToLive). UpdateTableReplicaAutoScaling was NOT:
   autoScalingSettingsFromInput built a fresh autoScalingSettings from only
   the current call's fields and assigned it wholesale over
   table.AutoScaling, so a call updating only GSI autoscaling silently wiped
   previously-set write-capacity settings and vice versa (this is actually
   c8ge's shape -- Update-vs-previous-Update, no Create op -- found while
   executing 1vv2's receiver-scope task). Fixed: merge into existing
   table.AutoScaling instead of replacing. Test:
   TestUpdateTableReplicaAutoScaling_WriteAndGSIUpdatesDontClobberEachOther,
   hand-verified to fail against unfixed code, hand-reverted and restored
   byte-identical.

2. Modify*/Put*/Set* verb families across ~155 services. AST pass (type-
   checked via go/packages, not text heuristics) over every Modify/Put/Set
   method on *InMemoryBackend/*InMemoryDB: 717+9 candidate funcs. Five
   detectors (wholesale struct/map assign of a bare param, unconditional
   pointer-field copy, composite-literal replacement of an already-read
   slot, maps.Clone/slices.Clone-mediated replace) surfaced 22 real hits
   across cloudwatchlogs/glue/kinesis/s3control/sesv2/ssm/
   applicationautoscaling/appsync/ssoadmin (sagemaker excluded -- a
   concurrent agent had it dirty mid-edit all session). Every hit read by
   hand against the real SDK: all 22 are legitimate. Several are
   doc-confirmed wholesale-replace-by-design (appsync
   PutGraphqlApiEnvironmentVariables: "each call ... will result in the
   overwriting of the existing environmental variable list ... you must
   include all existing and new environmental variables ... each time";
   s3control's three Put*Tagging ops: standard S3 full-tag-set-replace
   convention), others are already-correct merges the code comments
   document as intentional (ssoadmin PutApplicationAccessScope, glue
   PutAsset, sesv2's five Put*Attributes ops), one (ssm PutComplianceItems)

   detector false positive (fresh per-call slice, not stored state).

Net: real candidate count across both gaps was 9 + 22 = 31 (not ~37 by
