title: [bug] Go field types that emit the wrong JSON kind, which the SDK deserializer rejects outright
notes:
Generalises three separate instances this session, each found by accident
while looking for something else. The class is broader than timestamps and
has never been swept.

THE CLASS. A gopherstack struct field's Go type marshals to a JSON kind the
op's own generated deserializer refuses. The SDK does not coerce: it type-
switches and errors. So the call fails OUTRIGHT for every real client --
this is not a dropped field or a wrong value, it is an unusable operation.

CONFIRMED INSTANCES, all now fixed:

1. ssm PatchStatus.ApprovalDate -- string (RFC3339) where the deserializer
   reads `case json.Number` via ParseEpochSeconds (f56e519d7).
2. inspector2 Finding.Severity -- emitted as an object {label, score} where
   types.Severity is a bare string enum; ListFindings errored with "expected
   Severity to be of type string, got map[string]interface {} instead"
   (3e6dad409).
3. ssm ParameterMetadata.Policies -- a raw string where the member is
   []ParameterInlinePolicy, so the client's unmarshal failed (cee6106a9).

Note the three differ in direction: string-where-number, object-where-string,
string-where-list. A sweep keyed on any one shape misses the other two.

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT. A raw-body test asserts whatever the handler already
emits, so it passes. The field is present, plausibly named, and often carries
a sensible-looking value -- every field-presence audit this campaign runs
reports it clean. Only decoding through the real SDK client fails.

RELATED BUT ALREADY DONE, do not redo: gopherstack-5mr2 (request-side
epoch decode) and gopherstack-nc8s (response-side map[string]any bypassing a
type's MarshalJSON). Both were timestamp-specific and both are closed. This
issue is the general type-kind mismatch, timestamps included but not limited
to them.

METHOD. Do NOT grep. Two grep-derived scopes this session were wrong -- one
100% false positives, one 11x low. The tractable approach is to compare, per
op, the JSON kind gopherstack's response type marshals to against the kind
the pinned SDK's deserializer accepts for that member. The deserializers are
mechanical: each member is a `case "name":` followed by a type switch naming
the expected kind (json.Number, string, []interface{}, map[string]interface{}).
A tool that extracts the expected kind per member and compares it against the
Go field's marshalled kind would cover the class; the per-op deserializer is
the authority, not the type declaration, since format overrides exist.

BEWARE: a member can legitimately be a string under a protocol whose default
is numeric -- redshiftserverless GetIdentityCenterAuthToken.expirationTime is
awsjson1.1 and still expects a date-time string, verified in gopherstack-nc8s.
Read the member's own deserializer case, never infer from the protocol.

PROOF STANDARD: a real-SDK-client round trip that DECODES the response. A
raw-body assertion cannot fail on this class by construction.
close_reason:
Built a mechanical comparison tool (SDK deserializer-expected kind, parsed from deserializers.go's case+type-switch across 145 JSON-protocol services, vs gopherstack's json-tagged struct-field kind, matched by exact real-AWS-struct-name correspondence) rather than grepping. 242 high-confidence hits triaged by hand in full: 163 time.Time-typed (down to 19 needing individual reads after a helper-call heuristic, all 19 resolved -- 14 already correctly converted via an epoch helper the heuristic missed, 5 genuinely dead/unassigned fields), 79 other-kind hits (26 resolved via custom MarshalJSON the tool doesn't see, ~40 resolved as domain-vs-wire-projection false positives on manual read, 4 were a tool bug -- []byte marshals as base64 string in Go, not the array my extractor assumed).

8 real, live, confirmed instances fixed, each proven via a real aws-sdk-go-v2 client round-trip test, hand-reverted to confirm the exact predicted SDK error text, and restored md5sum-identical:
- codecommit PullRequestEvent.EventDate: string(RFC3339) -> time.Time/epoch (DescribePullRequestEvents always fails once any event exists)
- firehose MSKSourceConfiguration/MSKSourceDescription.ReadFromTimestamp: string -> float64, BOTH request and response sides share one struct (CreateDeliveryStream request-decode failure, the mirror-image of this issue's response-side framing, found incidentally)
- appsync Resolver.PipelineConfig: bare array -> {functions:[...]} object, via MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON keeping the Go field []string for internal/test use
- ecr ImageScanFinding.Attributes: map[string]string -> []Attribute (always populated by BASIC scans)
- athena CalculationStatistics.Progress: int64(hardcoded 100) -> string
- mediaconvert Job.LastShareDetails: {shareToken,sharedAt} object -> bare string, via MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON
- pipes BatchContainerOverrides.Environment: map[string]string -> []BatchEnvironmentVariable, both directions (same shared type)
- sagemaker TrainingPlanExtension{ExtendedAt,StartDate,EndDate}/TrainingPlanExtensionOffering{StartDate,EndDate}: time.Time -> epoch, via the same alias-embedding pattern this file already used for TrainingPlan/ReservedCapacity but missed for these two sibling types

Every candidate examined and rejected is documented with its reason in the session report (domain-vs-wire-projection duplicates, custom-MarshalJSON resolutions, and 7 genuinely dead/unreachable fields filed as gopherstack-fqtw). Structurally out-of-reach surface (19 XML/query-protocol services, cloudwatch's schema-codegen, appstream's rpc-v2-cbor, the 567-item low-confidence bucket, and ad hoc map[string]any construction sites with no automated coverage) filed as gopherstack-g479 for the next pass. PARITY.md updated inline (dated 2026-08-21) for all 8 services. Gates green: go build ./..., go vet -tags e2e/-tags integration ./..., gofmt, go test -race, golangci-lint (0 issues) on every touched service.

title: [bug] resources set to a transitional status that nothing ever advances, so clients poll forever
notes:
Two confirmed instances, both found by the gopherstack-oc9v sagemaker sweep,
both fixed: ClusterSchedulerConfig (c89f40af1) and InferenceComponent
(f7b2f9192). In each case the resource was stamped Creating at construction
and nothing in the backend ever advanced it -- no ticker, no goroutine, no
transition on a later call -- while a SIBLING RESOURCE IN THE SAME FILE
reached its terminal state correctly. That contrast is what made both
visible; a service where everything is stuck looks internally consistent.

WHY IT MATTERS: a client polling for readiness never exits its loop. The
emulator answers 200 with a well-formed body every time, so nothing looks
broken from the wire's point of view. This is invisible to every audit this
campaign runs -- the field is present, correctly named, correctly typed, and
carries a legal enum value.

WHY EXISTING TESTS DO NOT CATCH IT: InferenceComponent's lifecycle test
asserted Creating immediately after create -- which is TRUE -- and never
checked the status changed. An assertion that only tests the first moment
cannot catch a machine that never moves. Expect the same shape elsewhere:
look for lifecycle tests that assert the initial state and stop.

SIZING, deliberately rough. A first grep over services/*/*.go (excluding
tests) finds transitional literals concentrated in about 15 services:

    "IN_PROGRESS"      39        statusInProgress   17
    statusCreating     17        "InProgress"       16
    "PENDING"          12        "CREATING"          7
    statusDeleting      6

That is a count of ASSIGNMENTS, not of bugs. Most will be correct -- either
advanced elsewhere, or genuinely terminal for an emulator that does no real
work. Do not quote it as a defect figure; it is a starting set.

THE CHECK, per resource: find where the transitional value is written, then
establish whether ANY code path can replace it. A stamp with no writer is the
bug. Where the transition is genuinely unmodelable -- no async work exists to
complete -- the honest answer may be to stamp the terminal state at creation
rather than a lie about being in progress, or to disclose it in PARITY.md.
Decide per resource and say which.

BEWARE THE OPPOSITE ERROR: some resources SHOULD stay in a transitional state
because the op that advances them is one a client must call
(StartX/StopX/CompleteX). Trace the callers before declaring a stamp orphaned
-- an advancing path that exists but is rarely exercised is not the same as
one that does not exist.

Related: gopherstack-oc9v (found both instances).
close_reason: Both sweeps complete: 9 resources fixed across eks/glue/backup/bedrock/redshift/sagemaker (955af8951), then the four confirmed-and-left bugs in omics/inspector2/securityhub/cognitoidp. Every fix reuses the service's own mechanism — b.work.After, existing reconcilers, janitor ticks, runDelayed, or the reap-on-read pollCount overlay — and no timer was invented to fake progress. Two resources are disclosed as genuinely unmodelable (eventbridge PartnerEventSource needs an association this backend does not model; ecs AgentUpdateStatus reflects an agent that does not exist here). IMPORTANT CORRECTION for anyone reading the first sweep's notes: it reported omics as five files with 'no async mechanism anywhere in the package'. Four of the five were already correct, advancing on first read through a pollCount overlay in their own Get, fixed weeks earlier in efc42cbc4/69bbb940a. A search for tickers, goroutines and janitors cannot see a reap-on-read. Only shares.go was genuinely stuck. Four lifecycle tests across the two sweeps asserted a transitional status and stopped — two of them named after the terminal state they never checked. Also recorded: an ephemeral transitional value returned after a synchronous delete is not this bug, and several were correctly cleared on that basis.

title: [bug] hand-built map[string]any responses bypass a type's MarshalJSON, re-emitting timestamps as RFC3339 strings
notes:
Found 2026-08-21 by the gopherstack-oc9v sagemaker pass (22491c31e). This is
the RESPONSE-ENCODE twin of gopherstack-5mr2, which covered the
request-decode side.

THE MECHANISM. awsjson1.x expects timestamp members as epoch-second NUMBERS.
A domain type may carry a correct MarshalJSON that emits one -- sagemaker's
TrainingPlan does -- and a handler can still defeat it by hand-building the
response:

    m := map[string]any{"StartTime": plan.StartTime}   // *time.Time

encoding/json marshals time.Time via its own MarshalJSON, producing RFC3339:

    {"StartTime":"2025-08-21T12:40:00Z"}

so a real client fails with

    expected Timestamp to be a JSON Number, got string instead

Verified directly. ListTrainingPlans errored outright for any client with a
purchased plan.

WHY A CORRECT MarshalJSON DOES NOT SAVE YOU: it is only consulted when the
TYPE is marshalled. A map[string]any assembled field by field marshals each
value on its own, so the type's method never runs. The fix in sagemaker was
to route the summary through the type rather than rebuild it.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ISSUE RATHER THAN PART OF 5mr2: that sweep searched
decode paths -- json.Unmarshal, Decoder.Decode, echo Bind -- and found one
genuine instance. This is the encode side, and the search is different: look
for handlers assembling map[string]any (or anonymous structs) that assign a
time.Time or *time.Time directly, in services whose protocol is awsjson1.x or
restjson with number-format timestamps.

SEARCH GUIDANCE, learned from 5mr2's false positives: a grep for
`time.Time` in handler files finds mostly response STRUCTS with correct tags,
which are fine. The signal here is a time value flowing into a
map[string]any literal or an untyped assignment, not a struct field
declaration. 5mr2's twelve-instance "floor" turned out to be entirely false
positives for exactly this reason -- a type-checked walk found the real
instance in a service the grep never named. Prefer go/packages over regex.

BEFORE FIXING ANY INSTANCE, confirm the op's own serializer emits a number.
Query/XML services, header-bound members and http-date or date-time formats
are legitimately strings. Match the wire, do not normalise the Go types.

PROOF STANDARD: a real-SDK-client round trip that decodes the response.
A raw-body test cannot catch this -- it asserts whatever string the handler
already emits.

Related: gopherstack-5mr2 (request side), gopherstack-oc9v (found it).
close_reason: Swept, zero further instances. The sagemaker fix in 22491c31e remains the only occurrence in the tree. Method: a type-checked go/packages analyzer over all 164 service packages (zero load errors, ssm included and clean), flagging time.Time/*time.Time flowing into map[string]any literals or index-assignments, any-typed struct fields, and []any literals/appends — resolving the static type of both source and destination, so it cannot be fooled by correctly-tagged response structs, which is the false-positive class that sank the grep-derived floors in 5mr2 and my own sizing here. Seven candidate sites surfaced (bedrockagent PrepareAgent.PreparedAt; dlm GetLifecyclePolicy.DateCreated/DateModified; omics GetBatch creationTime/submittedTime/processedTime; redshiftserverless GetIdentityCenterAuthToken.expirationTime) and ALL SEVEN ARE ALREADY CORRECT: each op's own deserializer requires a JSON string for that member via a date-time/DateTimestamp format override, and encoding/json's default time.Time marshalling emits exactly RFC3339. The redshiftserverless case is the sharpest: it is awsjson1.1, where the protocol default is epoch-seconds, and the member still overrides to string — verified directly (expected Timestamp to be of type string, parsed via smithytime.ParseDateTime). Applying 'awsjson1.1 implies numbers' would have broken all seven working sites. No code changed, so nothing to gate or revert. Adjacent naming drift flagged, not fixed: omics' handleGetRunBatch/GetRunBatchSummary implement the real op GetBatch, and no GetRunBatch exists in the pinned SDK.

title: [bug] request structs decoding epoch-number timestamps into time.Time reject the whole request body
notes:
Found 2026-08-21 by the gopherstack-oc9v sagemaker pass, which discovered the
r80d/oc9v campaign had itself introduced this into five ops across four
separate commits before anyone noticed (fixed in fd65c414d).

THE MECHANISM. awsjson1.x and restjson serialize timestamp members as
epoch-second NUMBERS:

    ok.Double(smithytime.FormatEpochSeconds(*v.CreationTimeAfter))

Go's encoding/json cannot unmarshal a bare number into time.Time. It returns

    Time.UnmarshalJSON: input is not a JSON string

and that error fails the ENTIRE request body, not just the offending field.
So an op whose request struct declares

    CreationTimeAfter *time.Time `json:"CreationTimeAfter"`

returns 400 for any real client that sets that filter. The op is not
degraded, it is unusable -- and only for clients that exercise the field,
which is why it survives a green suite.

Verified by direct repro:
    json.Unmarshal([]byte(`{"t":1755780000}`), &struct{T *time.Time `json:"t"`}{})
    -> Time.UnmarshalJSON: input is not a JSON string

THE CORRECT PATTERN already exists in-repo. services/sagemaker/handler.go and
ai_recommendation_jobs.go use *float64 plus a timeFromEpochSecondsPtr helper.
The broken code simply did not copy it.

SIZING, deliberately rough rather than asserted: a first grep over
services/*/handler*.go finds 12 such fields across 4 services --
apigatewaymanagementapi, eventbridge, omics, redshift. That grep only covers
handler*.go and only matches one declaration style, so treat it as a floor,
not a count. Non-handler files declaring request structs, and any service
using a different field layout, are not covered by it.

WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH A SWEEP RATHER THAN FOUR FIXES: the campaign proved the
failure is invisible to the tests people actually write. Five passes each
added a time filter, each wrote a filter test, and not one populated the time
field -- so five green suites agreed with a parser that rejected every real
call. Any fix here needs a test that actually sets the timestamp through a
real SDK client.

BEFORE FIXING ANY INSTANCE, check the protocol. A query/XML service, or a
restjson member bound to a header or a timestampFormat of http-date or
date-time, may legitimately be a string. Read the op's own serializer and
confirm it emits a number before changing anything -- the point is to match
the wire, not to apply *float64 everywhere.

Related: gopherstack-oc9v (found it), gopherstack-r80d (same campaign).
close_reason: Fixed in the pipes commit. The one genuine remaining instance was KinesisStreamSourceParameters.StartingPositionTimestamp — restjson1, body-bound, serializer emits ok.Double(FormatEpochSeconds(...)) at serializers.go:1904 — so CreatePipe rejected the whole body and DescribePipe emitted RFC3339 where a number is expected. Fixed via the alias-embedding Marshal/Unmarshal pair used in eventbridge and cloudtrail, since the struct is shared across the decode target, the domain model, the response and the persistence snapshot. MY FLOOR OF 12 WAS ENTIRELY FALSE POSITIVES: all twelve fields in apigatewaymanagementapi, eventbridge, omics and redshift are response-encoding structs no client body decodes into — omics' runBatchListItemWire is the shape of the error, a response mirror matched by a grep that cannot tell direction. Real scope was one field in a service the grep never named, found by a type-checked go/packages analyzer walking every Unmarshal/Decode/Bind site across 164 packages including generic decode helpers. UpdatePipe deliberately untouched: the real UpdatePipeSourceKinesisStreamParameters declares no such member. Already-fixed instances confirmed in cloudtrail, eventbridge and sagemaker; kinesis' ShardIterator.CreatedAt is a self-issued opaque token, not wire-facing.

title: [bug] gendocs silently drops PARITY.md ops written in block style, under-reporting the audited count
notes:
Found 2026-08-21 while regenerating docs after the r80d batch-10 stepfunctions
pass.

SYMPTOM: the repo-wide operations badge went DOWN by one (6285 -> 6284) after
a pass that only ADDED fields. services/stepfunctions/README.md moved from
"26 (26 ok)" to "25 (25 ok)".

CAUSE: exactly one op entry had been rewritten from the repo's inline
convention

    GetExecutionHistory: {wire: ok, errors: ok, state: ok, persist: ok, note: "..."}

into YAML block style

    GetExecutionHistory:
      wire: fixed
      errors: ok
      ...

The ops list itself was unchanged -- 37 entries, identical names, verified
before and after. Converting that one entry back to inline restored the count
to 26 and made the badge diff disappear. So cmd/gendocs' manifest parser
reads inline maps only and skips block-style entries without complaint.

NOT a status-vocabulary problem: `fixed` is explicitly recognised at
cmd/gendocs/model.go:128 (`case "ok", "clean", "fixed"`) and 56 services
already use `wire: fixed`. The format is the whole cause.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ONE COUNT: this fails silently and in the direction
that looks like progress. A manifest can be materially correct while the
generated README under-reports it, and nothing errors. Every service's
manifest is hand-edited by agents who have no reason to know inline is
load-bearing -- block style is ordinary, valid YAML and is what an editor
reaches for when a note gets long. This will recur.

FIX, in preference order:
1. Make the parser accept both forms. Block style is valid YAML and the
   manifests are YAML; there is no good reason to reject it.
2. Failing that, make an unparseable or skipped op entry a hard ERROR rather
   than a silent omission -- the same principle as cmd/opcensus'
   ERROR-row change (gopherstack-c7s3), where a silently-empty result was
   indistinguishable from a legitimately small one.

Do NOT fix this by documenting "always use inline" and relying on that. The
convention is invisible at the point of editing, and this campaign has
repeatedly shown that a rule which is only written down gets violated by the
next pass.

Note the same manifest carried `last_audit_commit: pending (uncommitted this
pass -- see git log at merge time)`, which is the gopherstack-33in placeholder
class -- fixed in passing to b989093b4.

Related: gopherstack-33in (placeholder stamps), gopherstack-c7s3 (silent-empty
tooling results), gopherstack-r80d (the pass that surfaced it).
close_reason: Fixed. Parser now accepts block-style op entries alongside inline, and anything still unparseable fails the run with a nonzero exit rather than being skipped silently (same principle as opcensus' ERROR rows). Scale was 11x the issue's description: stepfunctions' manifest declares 37 ops and the parser found 26 — the issue was filed over one op, and the 37-vs-26 gap was visible during that investigation but dismissed as 'gendocs must only count certain ops' instead of chased. cloudwatch was dropping one. Kept hand-rolled deliberately: note: fields are unquoted free text with commas/colons/braces inside flow maps, so a real YAML parser rejects the corpus. Two false positives found by scanning the whole corpus — redshiftdata's folded note (handled via the YAML fold indicator) and iam/shield's ad-hoc changelog lists inside ops: (guarded by a lookahead for a real wire:/errors: field). An early brace-counting design regressed on sagemaker's manifest, which is missing a closing brace that the old parser tolerated by never checking balance. Docs are correspondingly not a no-op: stepfunctions 26->37, cloudwatch 49->50, medialive/opensearch gain silently-absent Feature families rows, badge 6285->6297, all corrections; iam byte-unchanged.

title: [bug] bedrock CreateEvaluationJob 400s for any real client: evaluationConfig/inferenceConfig are unions, the parser expects a flat shape
notes:
Found 2026-08-20 during the gopherstack-r80d batch 6 sweep of bedrock, as an
adjacent discovery rather than part of that cut. Recorded because it is more
severe than any of the nine required-output bugs fixed alongside it
(adb89e75f).

THE SHAPE. bedrock@v1.66.4 models CreateEvaluationJobInput's
evaluationConfig and inferenceConfig as POLYMORPHIC UNIONS
(types.EvaluationConfig / types.EvaluationInferenceConfig -- interface types
with concrete member variants). gopherstack's request parser expects a flat
array/object shape instead.

CONSEQUENCE: a real SDK client calling CreateEvaluationJob with genuine union
content gets a 400 today. Not a silently dropped field, not a zero value on
decode -- the call fails outright. This is independent of the required-output
fixes in the same commit and is not fixed by them.

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX, and why it was filed rather than rushed: union
deserialization is a distinct wire mechanism. smithy-go encodes a union as a
single-key object naming the variant, and the parser has to dispatch on that
key rather than read a fixed set of fields. Doing it properly means modelling
the variants, not widening the existing struct until the payload fits.

BEFORE FIXING, verify against the pinned SDK rather than this note: read
types.EvaluationConfig and types.EvaluationInferenceConfig, enumerate the
concrete variants and confirm which are actually reachable for the job types
gopherstack supports. Prove it with a real-SDK-client test that constructs a
union value -- a raw-body test cannot exercise the client's own union
encoder, which is the thing that breaks here.

RELATED GAP disclosed in the same pass, deliberately not fixed:
GetEvaluationJob.JobType is required on the response and has nothing to
derive it from -- real AWS reads it from a union gopherstack does not model.
That is the same root cause seen from the response side, so whoever fixes the
unions should check whether JobType falls out for free.

Both are recorded in services/bedrock/PARITY.md's gaps entry.

Related: gopherstack-r80d (the cut that surfaced it).
close_reason: Fixed. CreateEvaluationJob returned 400 ValidationException for any real client sending union content; reproduced before the fix and again on hand-revert for both Automated/Models and Human/RagConfigs. Unions now dispatch on the variant key as smithy-go encodes them, rather than widening a struct to fit. A second independent reachability bug found in the same code and not in the issue: gopherstack emitted ragConfig singular where AWS uses ragConfigs (serializers.go:10807) — fixing only the unions would have left the op broken and looking fixed. GetEvaluationJob.JobType is now derivable and emitted: EvaluationJobType is literally Automated/Human, the same tag naming the EvaluationConfig variant, so the earlier disclosure is withdrawn. CustomMetricConfig and the RAGConfig variant payloads are stored as opaque verbatim bytes and disclosed — the evaluation store is inert, so modelling the 12-variant recursive RetrievalFilter would be surface area nothing reads. Gates: go build ./..., both tagged vets, race tests, golangci-lint 0 issues.

title: [bug] omics Accept/Delete/CreateShare marshal the whole Share struct where the real outputs declare one member (three for Create)
notes:
Found 2026-08-20 re-verifying gopherstack-dv4s. Confirmed against omics@v1.49.5
and the code, not inferred.

THE REAL OUTPUT SHAPES:
  AcceptShareOutput  -> Status                       (one member)
  DeleteShareOutput  -> Status                       (one member)
  CreateShareOutput  -> ShareId, ShareName, Status   (three)
  GetShareOutput     -> Share *types.ShareDetails    (the full object -- correct here)

WHAT GOPHERSTACK DOES (services/omics/handler_shares.go:9-45): all three
handlers do `c.JSON(status, share)` on the full Share struct returned by the
backend. So Accept and Delete emit an entire share object where a real client
reads a single status field, and Create emits the same where three members
are declared.

This is the gopherstack-dv4s over-wide class, with the usual caveat that
makes it slippery: AN SDK-DRIVEN TEST CANNOT DETECT IT. The deserializer
silently discards keys it does not recognise, so driving the real client --
the technique that proves every missing-or-misnamed-field fix -- passes
happily against this bug. It needs a raw-body test asserting the extra keys
are ABSENT.

HOW IT SURVIVED: services/omics/PARITY.md's Share entry carried the "extra
fields on List summaries are harmless" note -- the same true-premise,
false-conclusion argument dv4s exists to eliminate, already removed from
personalize, appconfig and emrserverless. Here it was not excusing a stale
finding; it was excusing this live one. The rationale is now corrected in
place (0358610a2); the leak is not fixed.

FIX: give each of the three handlers its own response struct rather than
marshalling the domain object. Read each output type's declaration
separately -- do not derive one shape and apply it to the sibling ops. Accept
and Delete look identical and are, but Create is not, and GetShare
legitimately returns the whole object, so a blanket "narrow the Share
response" change would break it.

Note the status value itself needs checking while there: types.ShareStatus is
an enum, and the campaign's standing checks include verifying enum constants
in both directions rather than assuming the stored string is a legal value.

Related: gopherstack-dv4s (the class and the false rationale), gopherstack-xs7l
and gopherstack-tuh5 (the same note in two other manifests).
close_reason: Fixed in fc221c910. Accept/DeleteShare now emit status only; CreateShare emits shareId/shareName/status; GetShare deliberately unchanged and confirmed byte-identical — its OpDocument helper is live (called with &output, case 'share'), so its wrapper key is genuine, which is why this had to be three separate response shapes rather than one narrowing applied four times. Test is raw-body with ElementsMatch on the complete key set, so any extra key fails; an SDK-driven test cannot detect this class at all. Hand-revert reproduced the leak on all three ops while the GetShare guard stayed green. types.ShareStatus checked both directions: the backend writes only PENDING, ACTIVATING and DELETED, all legal SDK constants, no invented values. golangci-lint could not run — a concurrent agent held the lock across ~14 attempts — so it is deferred to the pre-push pass, not claimed.

title: [bug] CI lint installs golangci-lint latest, unpinned — v2.13.1 turned every open PR red on code nobody touched
notes:
Found 2026-08-20 while checking why three open PRs (2430, 2431, 2432) were
BLOCKED despite green local gates.

.github/workflows/ci.yml:70 pins the ACTION by sha
(golangci/golangci-lint-action@ba0d7d2 # v9) but does not pin the TOOL. The
action installs the newest golangci-lint release. Run 32440908060 logs it:

    Installing golangci-lint binary v2.13.1...
    Running [.../golangci-lint run] in [.../gopherstack]

Local dev is on 2.12.2 (`make install-deps` installs @latest via go install,
or brew -- also unpinned, so two developers on different days get different
linters). Result today:

    local  golangci-lint run ./test/integration/...  ->  0 issues
    CI     golangci-lint run                          ->  109 issues

109 = goimports 1, modernize 50, nolintlint 7, nonamedreturns 1,
staticcheck 50. Sample: test/integration/iotanalytics_test.go:381 SA1019,
iotanalytics deprecated by AWS.

NOT CAUSED BY THE PRs IT BLOCKS. `git diff --stat origin/main...<branch> --
test/` is empty for both 2431 and the pipes branch -- the flagged files are
untouched by either. Recently merged PRs (2425, 2426, 2429) show no failing
checks because they merged before 2.13.1 shipped and kept their historical
result. Every PR opened from now on hits this.

TWO SEPARATE PROBLEMS, DO NOT CONFLATE:

1. CI is not reproducible. A tool version arriving from the internet decides
   whether the repo builds. This is the actual defect and it recurs on every
   golangci-lint release. Fix: pin the version explicitly in the action
   (`with: version: vX.Y.Z`) AND make `make install-deps` install that same
   version instead of @latest, so local and CI agree by construction. The two
   must be pinned together or the gap reopens.

2. There are 109 real findings under 2.13.1. Pinning to 2.12.2 makes CI green
   but does NOT make them go away -- it defers them. File the upgrade as its
   own piece of work: bump the pin, fix the findings, land it deliberately.
   Do not silently sit on 2.12.2 forever and call the problem solved.

Sequence matters: pin first (small, unblocks three PRs, restores
determinism), upgrade second (large, real work). Pinning is not the fix for
the findings, only for the nondeterminism.

Note the findings live in build-tagged files (test/integration, test/e2e),
which is the same blind spot as gopherstack-0bpp -- code CI compiles but
tooling routinely fails to look at.
close_reason: Fixed in 5619eabb4. Makefile:10 holds GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION as the single source of truth; ci.yml and copilot-setup-steps.yml both grep that line and pass it to the action's version: input. install-deps now parses the installed version instead of testing for the binary's existence, so a developer already carrying 2.13.1 no longer silently keeps it; the unpinned brew path is dropped since brew cannot install an arbitrary historical version. Measured at repo root rather than the narrower path the issue cited: 2.12.2 gives 0 issues, 2.13.1 gives 109 with per-linter counts matching. The action's source at the pinned sha was read to confirm the input name and the required v prefix. This pins the version and does not fix the 109 findings — filed separately, deferred rather than dismissed.

title: [bug] pinpoint is 120-of-122 ops flat with dead helpers — the largest instance of the cnhp trap, and it was swept assuming otherwise
notes:
Surfaced 2026-08-20 by cmd/bodyclass (a7632d9a7), built for gopherstack-cnhp.

THE SHAPE. pinpoint has 122 operations. 120 are flat/payload -- the live
deserializer assigns straight into a single output member and the generated
deserializeOpDocument<Op>Output helper is DEAD. Two are void. Zero are
wrapped.

Verified by hand, not just by the tool:
  CreateApp's live path:
    err = awsRestjson1_deserializeDocumentApplicationResponse(
            &output.ApplicationResponse, shape)
  grep -c awsRestjson1_deserializeOpDocumentCreateAppOutput  ->  1
(one occurrence = its own definition, called by nothing)

WHY THIS IS P2 RATHER THAN A CURIOSITY. pinpoint WAS swept during the
gopherstack-6flj campaign -- it has a dated section in
services/_WRAPPER_KEY_SWEEP_REMAINDER.md. The campaign's core method was to
compare gopherstack's emitted top-level key against the SDK's deserializer.
On a service where every helper is dead, that comparison is meaningless: the
real client never reads a wrapper key at all, so both a "correct" and an
"incorrect" wrapper key produce the same result, and any finding recorded on
that basis is unreliable in EITHER direction.

That is exactly how appmesh acquired a fabricated "fixed" claim, and how a
glacier sweep nearly committed the same wrong fix. appmesh was mixed --
singular ops flat, List ops wrapped. pinpoint is the whole service.

WHAT TO DO.
1. Re-read pinpoint's sweep section. Any verdict that turns on a top-level
   wrapper key needs re-deriving against the flat shape; verdicts about
   per-item members, types, enums or nesting BELOW the top level are
   unaffected and still stand.
2. Run `go run ./cmd/bodyclass -service pinpoint` first, so the re-read starts
   from the real classification rather than the assumption.
3. Check whether any pinpoint fix landed during the campaign that moved a
   top-level key. If one did, it changed a key nothing reads -- harmless on
   the wire, but the manifest entry describing it is wrong and should be
   corrected rather than left as precedent.

THE OTHER 18 MIXED SERVICES worth the same one-command check before trusting
any wrapper-key verdict: apigateway, medialive, iotwireless, bedrock, omics,
apigatewayv2, lambda, appsync, lakeformation, appconfig, codeartifact,
appmesh, glacier, iotdataplane, bedrockruntime, polly, mediastoredata,
sagemakerruntime, appconfigdata.

RELATED: gopherstack-cnhp (the trap and the tool), gopherstack-1i5l
(manifests asserting verdicts the evidence does not support), gopherstack-6flj
(the campaign).
close_reason: Fixed in 1cca8edf1. bodyclass confirms 120 flat / 2 void / 0 wrapped, matching the issue exactly. The campaign's five pinpoint verdicts are all below the top level and remain valid — none turned on a wrapper key, so nothing it landed was inert and nothing needs withdrawal. The dead-helper trap cost nothing here. What it did cost: the campaign recorded Messaging and Phone as 'unchanged this pass', so those families were never diffed against the flat shape, and six ops had been implemented against the dead wrapper. Two were destructive — PutEvents dropped every event from a real client, and VerifyOTPMessage never received the code, falling through to a path that answers Valid for any code. Found by exhaustive grep of every bodyclass member name against every json tag in wire.go, not a spot check.

title: [bug] pipes: the top-level DeadLetterConfig is fabricated AND load-bearing, so real-shaped DLQ config silently never delivers
notes:
Found during the gopherstack-6flj sweep of pipes, 2026-08-20 (1316d6ed5).
Disclosed there, not fixed -- the rework is too large to do safely inside a
wire-shape pass.

THE SHAPE. Real CreatePipeInput, UpdatePipeInput and DescribePipeOutput have
NO top-level DeadLetterConfig member (verified against
aws-sdk-go-v2/service/pipes@v1.26.4). The real API carries it only nested:
  SourceParameters.KinesisStreamParameters.DeadLetterConfig
  SourceParameters.DynamoDBStreamParameters.DeadLetterConfig
gopherstack models BOTH nested locations correctly.

THE PROBLEM. gopherstack also carries a fabricated TOP-LEVEL DeadLetterConfig,
and the delivery path reads ONLY that one:
  services/pipes/runner.go:405-409
  services/pipes/sources_poll.go:268-274

So a client that configures a dead-letter queue the ONLY way the real API
allows -- nested under the source parameters -- gets a 200, sees its config
echoed back correctly from the nested field, and then silently never receives
a dead-lettered record. Failed events are dropped instead.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE USUAL FINDING. A prior audit noted the extra
top-level field and classified it as a harmless cosmetic extra, on the
correct general principle that real deserializers ignore unknown keys. That
principle holds for the RESPONSE. It does not hold here because the
fabricated field is also the one the BACKEND BEHAVIOUR keys off. An extra
field is cosmetic only if nothing reads it.

Worth generalising to the rest of this campaign: when a fabricated member is
found, grep for its READERS before classifying it as harmless. Fabricated
members that are also load-bearing invert the usual severity -- the wire looks
fine and the behaviour is wrong, which is the opposite of the silent-drop
class this sweep normally finds.

SCOPE OF THE FIX. Read the DLQ from the nested source parameters, keep the
top-level field as a deprecated alias or remove it, and update the delivery
path in both files above. It touches the runner, the persistence shape, and
roughly a dozen existing DLQ tests that construct the top-level form. Needs
its own pass with room to re-run the pipes suite properly.

RELATED: gopherstack-6flj (the sweep), gopherstack-1i5l (manifests recording
a surface as verified when it is not).
close_reason: Fixed in 2fc903c53. Both delivery sites now resolve the DLQ ARN through one helper reading SourceParameters.KinesisStreamParameters / .DynamoDBStreamParameters — verified those are the only two source types carrying a DLQ in pipes@v1.26.4; ActiveMQ, RabbitMQ, Kafka and SQS parameter types have none on either side. The fabricated top-level field is removed after grepping every reader and writer (wire parse, wire echo, the two buggy delivery sites; nothing in the UI, and persistence snapshots generically so old snapshots decode fine). Reproduction written first and confirmed failing before the fix. Separately: three existing DLQ tests were asserting an SQS-sourced pipe with a top-level DLQ — a configuration the real API cannot express, since PipeSourceSqsQueueParameters has only BatchSize and MaximumBatchingWindowInSeconds. All rewritten.

title: PARITY manifest last_audit_commit values point at unmerged branches, breaking the schema's own re-audit protocol
notes:
RESOLUTION FOR THIS SESSION (2026-08-22), against the merged tree (#2430/#2432 landed).

=== cmd/stampaudit output, by category (go run ./cmd/stampaudit vs origin/main, 7d threshold) ===
  160 manifests audited
  140 resolved to a real local sha; 20 have no last_audit_commit field (the
      gopherstack-33in class -- confirmed cleared to empty, never prose, by this run)
  Of the 140 resolved:
    140/140 (100%) unreachable from origin/main -- CONFIRMS the structural claim below
     55/140 also fail the date test (gap > 7d)
     85/140 unreachable-only, date gap within 7d -- not flagged stale
      0 clean (unreachable is universal; nothing is both reachable+fresh)
  0 missing-object shas, 0 non-sha placeholders remaining.

=== direct verification against #2430/#2432 ===
Confirmed directly with git, not inferred: 4cb8d047c (#2430) and c1b8de09a (#2432)
are each single-parent commits on origin/main (4cb8d047c's sole parent is c1b8de09a;
c1b8de09a's sole parent is 1b0b3b8fd, #2429) -- i.e. real squash commits, each
collapsing a multi-commit branch into one. Also found a live example in this
session's own tree: services/accessanalyzer/PARITY.md cites last_audit_commit
c79ebf1b569b (dated 2026-08-21). That commit object exists locally, sits only on
fix/cfn-stack-policy-and-pinpoint (this branch), and `git merge-base --is-ancestor`
confirms it is NOT an ancestor of origin/main NOR of 4cb8d047c. Once this branch
itself is squash-merged, that citation becomes permanently unreachable too -- proving
"unreachable by construction," not "temporarily unreachable pending a merge."

=== RECOMMENDATION: keep last_audit_commit as informational provenance; last_audit_date is the real re-audit signal ===
Evidence: stampaudit's own numbers make the case better than argument does.
Reachability is 100% negative for EVERY resolved citation in the corpus (140/140) --
it carries zero discriminating information under this repo's squash-merge policy,
by construction, permanently. Meanwhile the date-gap test DOES discriminate (55
fail, 85 pass) -- it is the only signal in this dataset that ever produced a
real, confirmed finding (per the issue's own tally: 5 confirmed real cases,
appmesh/codeconnections/emrserverless/detective/sts, all found by the date test;
0 ever found by any sha/reachability-based test).

REJECTED: record merge-base + PR number instead. Two independent reasons:
1. Causality: neither a merge-base nor a PR number is knowable to the worker at
   audit-write time -- the merge-base depends on the target ref's tip AT MERGE TIME
   (which hasn't happened yet) and the PR number doesn't exist until a PR is opened.
   This reproduces exactly the gopherstack-33in failure mode (asking a worker for a
   value only the orchestrator can ever know), just with a differently-shaped
   placeholder next time.
2. Semantics: merge-base(sha, ref) is the point BEFORE the audit's own changes
   landed. `git diff <merge-base>..HEAD -- services/<svc>/` would include the
   audit's own diff as "drift," flagging every freshly-landed audit as stale on
   day one -- a systematic false positive, not a fix. (stampaudit's own merge-base
   suggestions already prove this isn't free: 40/140 suggested merge-bases still
   fail the date test outright, "STILL FAILS, do not use".)
Also rejected: mass-rewriting all 140 citations to their stampaudit-suggested
merge-base. Explicitly out of scope per this issue's own instruction, and would only
cosmetically fix the 85 unreachable-only rows while leaving the 55 genuinely-stale
ones exactly as stale (merge-base doesn't fix a stale date, it only fixes
reachability, which was never the actual problem).

Net: no schema change needed. last_audit_commit stays a bare-sha-or-empty field
(cmd/gendocs already enforces the shape) documenting "HEAD at write time" as
forensic provenance only, usable via `git show <sha>` for as long as the object
survives locally (not guaranteed indefinitely -- eligible for gc once truly
orphaned) but never as an operational `git diff` re-audit trigger. last_audit_date
plus stampaudit's date-gap predicate is the actual re-audit signal, and it already
works today without any manifest rewrite. Worth a doc-only follow-up (out of my
edit scope -- services/_PARITY_TEMPLATE.md is not services/*/PARITY.md) to stop the
template's "Re-audit protocol: git diff <last_audit_commit>..HEAD" comment from
instructing something that will structurally never work post-squash.

=== duplicate-key / annotated-token survivors: found MORE than the issue's estimate ===
Checked via a temporary in-package test (cmd/gendocs, deleted after use) that ran
ParseParityFile across all 160 real manifests and printed every Warning --
not a naive grep, the actual tolerant parser gendocs uses.
- Annotated-parenthetical-token class (the 18-file class from commit 7ee49835a):
  ZERO survivors anywhere in the corpus. Fully clean.
- Duplicate-key class: found 12 files / 29 warnings, not 4. The 4 the union merge
  produced with a placeholder value (HEAD, b451ad0d6+wt, "pending...") were already
  caught by the EXISTING non-sha/non-token validators and fixed in 7ee49835a. But
  gendocs had no duplicate-key check at all, so 12 files where BOTH copies were
  individually valid (two real shas, two "A" grades) survived silently: acm,
  amplify, appmesh, apprunner, codeconnections, mwaa, pipes, redshiftdata,
  scheduler, swf, timestreamquery -- last_audit_commit dup in 7, last_audit_date
  dup in 11, overall dup in 8, sdk_module dup in 1 (swf), and a fully duplicated
  ops: block (not just scalar keys) in 2 (amplify, scheduler).

Fixed 10 of 12 this session (acm, appmesh, apprunner, codeconnections, mwaa, pipes,
redshiftdata, swf, timestreamquery -- 9 scalar-only + appmesh, which turned out to
need the same treatment despite initially looking like the risky case) by keeping
whichever header's content is actually reflected in the file's single ops: block
(cross-checked, not guessed -- e.g. confirmed appmesh's ops notes literally quote
"not the dead OpDocument helper" from the 2026-08-19 block, not the 2026-08-21
r80d-batch block, before choosing which to keep) and dropping the stale duplicate,
same "duplicates dropped, cleaned values kept" precedent as commit 7ee49835a.
timestreamquery's discarded block was also truncated mid-sentence by the merge
(ends "Fixed LastRunSummary.RunStatus/") -- reconstructed losslessly by concatenating
with the surviving block's complete continuation of the same sentence, not rewritten.

Did NOT touch amplify/scheduler: these have two FULL ops: blocks with different

title: the OpDocument deserializer trap: single-payload restjson ops make the wrapper-key function dead code
notes:
SECOND CONFIRMED FIRING, and this time the safeguard worked. glacier sweep,
2026-08-20 (ea5c289af).

The agent read deserializeOpDocumentGetVaultAccessPolicyOutput and
deserializeOpDocumentGetVaultNotificationsOutput, saw their wrapper-key case
lists, and wrapped both responses under "policy"/"vaultNotificationConfig".
A real SDK round-trip test failed immediately with all-nil typed fields.
Reading each op's actual HandleDeserialize showed the live path:

  err = awsRestjson1_deserializeDocumentVaultNotificationConfig(
          &output.VaultNotificationConfig, shape)

Flat body. The helper is never called. Fully reverted; both round-trip tests
kept, so the flat shape is now pinned against a future pass making the same
inference.

WHAT ACTUALLY PREVENTED THE BAD COMMIT: the agent wrote the real-SDK
round-trip test BEFORE trusting its own wrapper-key reading. That ordering is
now the standing instruction in these sweep briefs, and it is the difference
between this and appmesh, where the same wrong inference was recorded as a
"fixed" claim in PARITY.md and survived until someone re-derived it.

RUNNING TALLY of how the trap resolves per service, which shows it is
genuinely per-op and cannot be answered by protocol alone:
  appmesh      restjson  singular ops FLAT (helper dead)      -> trap fired
  glacier      restjson  2 ops FLAT (helper dead)             -> trap fired
  amplify      restjson  DeleteApp WRAPPED (helper live)      -> no trap
  mediaconvert restjson  every body op WRAPPED (helper live)  -> no trap
  managedblockchain restjson every op WRAPPED (helper live)   -> no trap
  shield       awsjson11 always WRAPPED                       -> N/A
  kinesis      awsjson11 always WRAPPED                       -> N/A
  codestarconnections/codeconnections awsjson10 always WRAPPED -> N/A
Restjson is the only protocol where the question arises, and within restjson
it splits per-op inside the same service. Confirmed rule: awsjson1.x always
routes through the OpDocument helper, because the single-payload flattening
that orphans it is a restjson behaviour.
close_reason: Addressed in a7632d9a7 with cmd/bodyclass, which classifies each op's response body by AST-walking the deserializer's BODY rather than grepping its name. This issue's own prescribed check (grep -c on the helper, read the call site) is what produced the appmesh and glacier false positives it documents — three later cases defeat it: payload-bound ops call the helper with (output, response.Body, response.ContentLength), and polly/mediastoredata/appconfigdata all have helpers that are called and contain no JSON decode at all. Validated against all thirteen ground-truth cases from the campaign with zero disagreements, including appmesh (flat singular, wrapped List) against amplify DeleteApp (wrapped, same protocol) — the pair proving it is per-op. Fleet-wide: 6247 wrapped, 175 flat/payload, 15 header-only, 1703 void, 2330 unknown of which 2324 are non-JSON protocols honestly declined and 6 are genuine event-stream ops. New finding filed as gopherstack-lffs: pinpoint is 120-of-122 flat with dead helpers and was swept assuming otherwise.

title: cross-service host-prefix reachability: mwaa/lakeformation/cloudwatchlogs/servicediscovery/sfn share Omics' Smithy hostPrefix gap
description:
While closing gopherstack-keee (Omics SDK client host-prefix reachability), grepped every pinned aws-sdk-go-v2 service module under go.mod for the same shape (`req.URL.Host = "..." + req.URL.Host`, the generated code for Smithy's `@endpoint(hostPrefix:)` trait). Five more services carry it, ALL implemented in gopherstack:

- `mwaa` (v1.43.4): 12 ops -- essentially its entire real surface (ListEnvironments, InvokeRestApi, CreateCliToken, DeleteEnvironment, GetEnvironment, UntagResource, ListTagsForResource, UpdateEnvironment, CreateEnvironment, PublishMetrics, CreateWebLoginToken, TagResource). Three prefixes, using "." not "-": `api.`, `env.`, `ops.`.
- `lakeformation` (v1.50.4): 5 ops (GetQueryState, GetWorkUnitResults, GetQueryStatistics, GetWorkUnits, StartQueryPlanning). Two prefixes: `query-`, `data-`.
- `cloudwatchlogs` (v1.81.1): 2 ops (GetLogObject, StartLiveTail). Prefix: `stream-`.
- `servicediscovery` (v1.43.4): 2 ops (DiscoverInstances, DiscoverInstancesRevision). Prefix: `data-`.
- `sfn`/stepfunctions (v1.45.4): 2 ops (TestState, StartSyncExecution). Prefix: `sync-`.

gopherstack-keee's own finding (see services/omics/PARITY.md's 2026-08-15 note) is that for Omics this does NOT require a gopherstack routing/auth code change: `pkgs/service/router.go` and every RouteMatcher in the repo match on URL.Path alone (confirmed by grep -- none of these five services' RouteMatchers reference `.Host` either), Omics' own 107 real (method,path) pairs have zero cross-prefix-family collisions, and SigV4 verification (`pkgs/httputils/sigv4.go:241`) derives its canonical "host" from whatever actually arrived, not an expected value. The unreachability is a pure client-side DNS/dial failure that happens before any byte reaches gopherstack (confirmed live: `dial tcp: lookup workflows-127.0.0.1 on 127.0.0.53:53: no such host`) -- there is nothing for gopherstack's Go code to fix.

That conclusion is very likely to hold for these five services too (same mechanism, same repo-wide path-only routing convention) but was NOT individually re-verified against each service's own RouteMatcher/op-path table this pass -- in particular mwaa is worth checking first since it's nearly its whole operation surface, not just a handful of ops. If any of the five DOES have a path collision that real AWS disambiguates only via one of these host prefixes (the s3/glacier vacuity-trap class), that would be a genuine routing bug distinct from Omics' finding.

Recommended next step: for each of the five, (1) extract every real op's (method,path) from its own serializers.go the way services/omics/handler_sdk_route_table_test.go and this pass's Omics test did, (2) confirm no two ops share a path, (3) confirm the service's RouteMatcher doesn't already assume Host disambiguates something, (4) if clean, add the same before/after SDK round-trip test pattern gopherstack-keee's services/omics/host_prefix_reachability_test.go established (real unmodified client fails to dial -> redial-to-real-listener transport succeeds despite the real, un-disabled host-prefix rewrite) as a permanent regression guard, one PR per service given mwaa alone is a near-full-surface pass.

## Context
discovered-from gopherstack-keee, session on branch chore/queue-2026-08-11
close_reason:
All five services investigated. No production code needed to change anywhere, and the counts in the filing were exactly right - the first time this campaign a recorded scope survived contact, after four that were wrong by large factors.

mwaa 12 ops across api., env. and ops. prefixes; lakeformation 5 across query- and data-; cloudwatchlogs 2 on stream-; servicediscovery 2 on data-; stepfunctions 2 on sync-. Every one cited to its api_op file and line.

No routing collisions, cross-prefix or cross-service. mwaa and lakeformation gate their whole RouteMatcher on the SigV4 service name and already appear in the confirmed-clean list in _ROUTE_COLLISIONS.md. The other three dispatch entirely on X-Amz-Target and never read Host or Path, so they are structurally immune. Same conclusion as omics: a per-op Smithy Finalize middleware causing a client-side dial failure, with nothing of ours involved.

THE REAL FINDING IS THE TEST COVERAGE. lakeformation's disableDataHostPrefix was applied to the whole client through APIOptions, silently disabling the rewrite for two ops beyond the one it was written for. mwaa had NO real-SDK-client tests at all - every test drives the handler over a raw recorder. The other three had real clients that never touched the affected ops. So across six services including omics, reachability was either masked or simply never proven either way.

All five now have host_prefix_reachability_test.go proving the unmodified client's behaviour in both directions.

CLOUDWATCHLOGS IS A DISCLOSED EXCEPTION. GetLogObject and StartLiveTail return Smithy event streams in real AWS while gopherstack returns unary JSON - already documented in the handler. Confirmed live that even with reachability fixed the client fails with 'unexpected output result type: nil'. Its test proves reachability, auth and routing through the error path and documents why no happy-path assertion is attempted. That gap is real and separate.

s3 virtual-hosted addressing verified still green rather than assumed.

title: omics real SDK client can't reach gopherstack for run/workflow/configuration ops -- host prefix unsupported
description:
Found as a side effect of gopherstack-op3e's route-collision sweep, not by looking for it.

Most of Omics' real API surface (ListConfigurations, CreateConfiguration, GetConfiguration, DeleteConfiguration, CreateWorkflow, CreateRunGroup, CancelRun, DeleteRun, GetRunCache, ListBatch, and more -- essentially the whole run/workflow/configuration family) is generated by aws-sdk-go-v2/service/omics with an unconditional client-side host rewrite: req.URL.Host = "workflows-" + req.URL.Host (see e.g. api_op_ListConfigurations.go, api_op_CreateWorkflow.go, and ~15 other api_op_*.go files in that module). This happens regardless of BaseEndpoint override.

gopherstack serves every service from one host with no workflows-<host> virtual-host routing implemented anywhere in services/omics or cli.go. Confirmed live: a real Omics SDK client's ListConfigurations call against a local httptest.Server captured the outgoing request and the Host header was rewritten to workflows-<original-host>, which fails DNS resolution for any endpoint that isn't behind a wildcard *.workflows-<domain> setup.

Net effect: for this whole operation family, a stock AWS SDK client cannot reach gopherstack at all today, independent of any RouteMatcher/routing bug. Two RouteMatcher collisions were found and fixed against this same path family this session (appconfigdata and inspector2 both over-claimed /configuration and /configuration/ respectively) -- both are real fixes, but neither is reachable by a stock SDK client until this host-prefix gap is also closed, so the two new regression tests in test/integration drive RouteMatcher() directly with a crafted Authorization header instead of a full SDK round trip.

Likely fix shape: same pattern sagemakerruntime already uses (services/sagemakerruntime/handler.go's RouteMatcher checks strings.HasPrefix(c.Request().Host, "runtime.sagemaker.") as an alternate match condition) -- omics would need an equivalent Host-prefix branch recognizing workflows-<anything> and either serving it from the same handler or documenting a required local /etc/hosts / dnsmasq wildcard setup for real-client testing. Needs research into whether gopherstack's local dev/docker setup can support wildcard host resolution at all before deciding the fix shape.

## Context
Discovered during gopherstack-op3e's second sweep pass while investigating the appconfigdata/omics and inspector2/omics /configuration collisions. See services/_ROUTE_COLLISIONS.md's 'Fixed this pass' section, item 2/3's closing note, for the live verification that established this.
close_reason:
Investigated and closed with a test, not a routing-code fix -- the real conclusion is there is no routing-layer bug to fix. Full writeup in services/omics/PARITY.md's 2026-08-15 note; summary:

Scope is larger than this issue's framing: ALL 107 real Omics ops carry a host-prefix rewrite (not just run/workflow/configuration), across FIVE literal prefixes -- workflows- (38), control-storage- (34), analytics- (28), storage- (4), tags- (3) -- confirmed by grepping every api_op_*.go in the pinned omics@v1.49.5 module. Mechanism: a per-operation Smithy Finalize-stage middleware (endpointPrefix_op<Op>Middleware, e.g. api_op_CancelRun.go:127, inserted after "ResolveEndpointV2"), the generated code for Smithy's @endpoint(hostPrefix:) trait -- not an endpoint resolver, not a static trait read once.

Not unique to Omics: grepping every pinned SDK module in go.mod found the same shape in mwaa (12 ops, nearly its whole surface), lakeformation (5), cloudwatchlogs (2), servicediscovery (2), and sfn/stepfunctions (2) -- all implemented in gopherstack. Filed gopherstack-3gbe to track those separately (P2), since that finding stands on its own regardless of what this issue does about Omics.

Established, live, that NO gopherstack routing or auth code needs to change: Handler.RouteMatcher (handler.go:223) matches on URL.Path alone; all 107 real (method,path) pairs are pairwise distinct across every prefix family (zero collisions, unlike s3's bucket-vs-path class); SigV4 verification (pkgs/httputils/sigv4.go:241) derives its canonical "host" from whatever actually arrived (r.Host), not a configured value. The reported unreachability is a pure client-side DNS/dial failure that happens before any byte reaches gopherstack -- confirmed live: "dial tcp: lookup workflows-127.0.0.1 on 127.0.0.53:53: no such host". There is nothing in pkgs/service/router.go or any RouteMatcher to fix; the sagemakerruntime-style Host-prefix RouteMatcher branch this issue speculated about would be dead code (Omics' routing is already 100% host-agnostic and correct).

Added services/omics/host_prefix_reachability_test.go: drives the real, UNMODIFIED aws-sdk-go-v2 omics client (not a hand-crafted request, and not the existing disableAnalyticsHostPrefix workaround every other round-trip test in this package already uses to sidestep this) through one representative op per prefix family. Before: proves the unmodified client can't dial. After: a redial-to-the-real-listener transport (same technique as services/s3control/handler_create_tags_test.go's per-account-ID-host workaround) lets the SDK's real, un-disabled host-prefix rewrite reach gopherstack anyway, and the op succeeds with correct decoded values -- proving gopherstack survives the rewrite. Scoped out: the four "storage-" ops need an existing store with real uploaded content, left for a future pass. Confirmed s3 virtual-hosted-style addressing and pkgs/..., pkgs/service/... remain green and untouched.

Gates all green: build, vet, race (services/omics, pkgs/..., pkgs/service/...), go fix -diff (no diff), golangci-lint (0 findings, no banned nolints).

Real-deployment implication (documented, not code): a production gopherstack endpoint real Omics clients must reach needs DNS coverage for the five prefixes (e.g. a wildcard record) -- same class of requirement s3 virtual-hosted addressing and CloudFront KeyValueStore's per-account-ID host already impose.

title: cross-service RouteMatcher collisions: inspector2 and macie2 swallowed securityhub's /findings and /members
description:
Found as a side effect of gopherstack-n3zi (real-client round-trip coverage for securityhub).

securityhub's BatchImportFindings (POST /findings/import), GetFindings (POST /findings),
BatchUpdateFindings, GetFindingHistory, CreateMembers (POST /members), GetMembers,
ListMembers, DeleteMembers, InviteMembers and DisassociateMembers were ALL unreachable
over the real HTTP wire, despite being fully implemented and unit-tested (unit tests call
h.Handler() directly, bypassing RouteMatcher entirely, so they never caught this).

Root cause: inspector2's RouteMatcher claims any path with prefix "/findings/" or
"/members/" unconditionally; macie2's claims "/findings" and "/members" unconditionally.
Both are registered in cli.go before securityhub, and pkgs/service/router.go routes to
the first matcher that returns true (ties broken by registration order) -- so a real
securityhub client's BatchImportFindings request got intercepted by inspector2 and
returned 501 NotImplementedException, and CreateMembers got intercepted by macie2's
CreateMember and returned 400 ValidationException. securityhub's own handler never ran.

Confirmed via a live docker-based test/integration run: before the fix, both requests
failed with exactly those wrong-service errors; after, they succeed and reach securityhub.

FIX APPLIED (this pass): gated inspector2's "/findings/" and "/members/" prefixes, and
macie2's "findings"/"members" prefixes, behind an Authorization-header signing-service
check (isInspector2Request / isMacie2Request), mirroring securityhub's own existing
isSecurityHubRequest pattern for its ambiguous /findings prefix. Per this repo's own
route-collision precedent (never fix by raising MatchPriority -- see the closed
gopherstack-sokq bedrockagent issue), this is the correct fix, not a priority bump.

REMAINING SCOPE: I only checked services whose handler code contained the literal
strings "findings"/"members" (accessanalyzer, cleanrooms, guardduty, iot, macie2,
managedblockchain, quicksight, redshift, securityhub, inspector2) and hand-verified
guardduty is safe (its paths are nested under /detector/{id}/... rather than a bare
prefix). accessanalyzer, cleanrooms, iot, managedblockchain, quicksight and redshift
were NOT individually verified for collision -- their occurrences looked structurally
different (nested paths, JSON field names, not bare RouteMatcher prefixes) but this was
not confirmed the way inspector2/macie2 were.

More importantly, this is unlikely to be the only cross-service prefix collision in the
registry: 161 services each define their own RouteMatcher, mostly via string-prefix
tables, and pkgs/service/router.go's first-match-wins-by-registration-order semantics
means any two services sharing a bare top-level path segment (not just "findings"/
"members") can silently swallow each other with zero test signal, since unit tests almost
universally call h.Handler() directly rather than going through the shared Router. A
dedicated sweep -- enumerate every RouteMatcher's claimed prefixes across all 161
services, flag any prefix claimed unconditionally by 2+ services, and check whether the
narrower/later-registered one is actually disambiguated -- would likely find more.
close_reason: Closed

title: cloudformation UpdateStack never enforces the stored stack policy
description:
SetStackPolicy (services/cloudformation/stack_policy.go:4) stores a policy per stack in b.stackPolicies, and GetStackPolicy echoes it back verbatim -- but that echo is the only read path. UpdateStack (services/cloudformation/stacks.go) never references b.stackPolicies or StackPolicy at all (grep confirms zero hits outside store.go/persistence.go/stack_policy.go), so a policy that denies Update:* on a protected resource has no effect: the resource updates anyway.

Same shape as gopherstack-ygfk (sns AddPermission/Policy): state written by a handler (SetStackPolicy), persisted, and never consumed by the op whose behavior it is supposed to gate (UpdateStack). GetStackPolicy returning the raw stored value doesn't count -- it's an echo, not an application of the policy to influence another op.

Found via a bounded ygfk-pattern sweep of services/cloudformation and services/stepfunctions while closing out gopherstack-vc2g/1s2g (2026-08-14). Not fixed in that session: real fix requires parsing the stack policy document (Statement[].Effect/Action/Principal/Resource matching against LogicalResourceId) and checking it during UpdateStack's per-resource update path, plus honoring the StackPolicyDuringUpdateBody/StackPolicyDuringUpdateURL override on UpdateStack -- real feature work, not a wire-field swap.

## Context
discovered-from gopherstack-ygfk sweep, session on branch chore/queue-2026-08-11

Already fixed on main in commit 69bbb940a (PR #2417, 2026-08-15) as a side effect of closing the parent gopherstack-ygfk sweep -- checkStackPolicy (stack_policy.go) now parses and evaluates the stored policy per resource change during UpdateStack (stacks.go:588, before any state mutation), honors StackPolicyDuringUpdateBody as a non-persisted one-call override, and PARITY.md already documents the fix in detail. title: dynamodb: legacy Query/Scan filter params (KeyConditions/QueryFilter/ScanFilter) still silently dropped
description:
Follow-up from gopherstack-lze5: Expected/ConditionalOperator/AttributeUpdates (PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem) are now fixed by translating them into ConditionExpression/UpdateExpression and reusing the existing services/dynamodb/expr evaluator (see legacy_conditions.go, PARITY.md gaps entry). Query's KeyConditions and Query/Scan's QueryFilter/ScanFilter were deliberately left out of that pass and remain wire-undeclared -- a legacy client's ScanFilter/QueryFilter is silently dropped (Scan/Query returns unfiltered results) and KeyConditions is silently dropped (Query needs KeyConditionExpression instead).

Recommended approach: same translate-to-expression-string technique as the fixed half. QueryFilter/ScanFilter -> synthesize an equivalent FilterExpression (applied post-fetch, same evaluator path as the real FilterExpression already uses in item_ops_query.go/item_ops_scan.go) -- lower risk, no PK-extraction coupling. KeyConditions -> synthesize an equivalent KeyConditionExpression, but item_ops_query.go's filterCandidatesForKeyCondition/preParseQueryPKValue assume exprParts[0] (the first AND-clause) is the partition-key equality condition for its indexed-lookup fast path; a map-keyed legacy KeyConditions needs to be reordered against the table's KeySchema (partition key first, sort key second) before being joined into a string, which the Expected/AttributeUpdates translator didn't need to handle.
close_reason: Fixed: KeyConditions/QueryFilter/ScanFilter now implemented. Two layers: (1) models.QueryInput/ScanInput didn't declare these fields at all (same wire-drop class as the Put/Update/Delete half in lze5) -- added models.LegacyCondition + KeyConditions/QueryFilter/ScanFilter/ConditionalOperator wire fields, wired through convert_ops.go's toSDKLegacyConditions. (2) legacy_query_scan.go translates them into KeyConditionExpression/FilterExpression through the same evaluator paths, reusing legacy_conditions.go's renderComparison/placeholder machinery. KeySchema-reordering blocker solved: translateKeyConditionsToKeyConditionExpression looks up PK/SK by name against KeySchema and always emits [pk-clause, sk-clause] regardless of the legacy map's (nonexistent) order -- tested with sort key listed first in the Go map literal. Operator restrictions enforced (PK: EQ only; SK: EQ/LE/LT/GE/GT/BEGINS_WITH/BETWEEN, disclosed as our own transcription of the un-inlined AWS guide). Mutual exclusion vs modern expression params enforced per operation. Tests (legacy_query_scan_test.go) assert behaviour via real aws-sdk-go-v2 client, hand-reverted both fix layers independently to confirm each is load-bearing (byte-identical restore confirmed). All gates green: build/vet/race/go fix/golangci-lint(0 issues)/pkgs race tests. See PARITY.md gaps for full writeup and citations.

title: dynamodb: legacy pre-expression API parameters (Expected/ConditionalOperator/AttributeUpdates/KeyConditions/QueryFilter/ScanFilter) are silently dropped
description:
DynamoDB's legacy \"LegacyConditionalParameters\" API (pre-2013, predates
ExpressionAttributeNames/Values) is still a real, wire-serialized part of the
service (confirmed against dynamodb@v1.63.1's api_op_Query.go:92/284/316,
api_op_Scan.go, api_op_PutItem.go, api_op_UpdateItem.go, api_op_DeleteItem.go
-- the SDK's serializers.go genuinely writes "AttributesToGet",
"ConditionalOperator", "KeyConditions", "QueryFilter", "ScanFilter",
"AttributeUpdates", and "Expected" onto the wire when a caller sets those
SDK-struct fields, not just doc-comment references).

None of these fields exist anywhere in services/dynamodb/models/types.go
(QueryInput, ScanInput, PutItemInput, DeleteItemInput, UpdateItemInput), so a
real client using the legacy API has every one of these keys silently dropped
by json.Unmarshal on the way in -- 200 OK, err == nil, wrong behavior:

- ScanFilter / QueryFilter ignored -> Scan/Query returns MORE items than the
  caller's filter should have allowed (no filtering happens at all).
- AttributeUpdates ignored on UpdateItem with no UpdateExpression set -> the
  item is not updated at all; the caller believes it was.
- Expected / ConditionalOperator ignored on PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem ->
  the conditional check never happens; the write always succeeds even when a
  real DynamoDB client would get ConditionalCheckFailedException.
- KeyConditions ignored on Query with no KeyConditionExpression set -> query
  fails validation (wrong error) or behaves incorrectly if some expression
  happens to be present from another source.

Zero backend support exists for any of this today (confirmed: no reference
to ComparisonOperator/AttributeValueUpdate/ConditionalOperator anywhere in
services/dynamodb/*.go). This is not a small wire-drop fix like the
ReturnConsumedCapacity class fixed in 53cfd590b -- it requires implementing
the legacy Condition{ComparisonOperator, AttributeValueList} evaluation
(EQ/NE/LE/LT/GE/GT/NOT_NULL/NULL/CONTAINS/NOT_CONTAINS/BEGINS_WITH/IN/BETWEEN)
combined via ConditionalOperator (AND/OR), across Put/Update/Delete/Query/Scan.

A clean, low-risk implementation path: translate each legacy Condition into
an equivalent ConditionExpression/UpdateExpression fragment (with synthesized
ExpressionAttributeNames/Values) and feed it through the EXISTING expr/
evaluator (services/dynamodb/expr) rather than writing a second evaluation
engine -- this reuses already-proven expression logic instead of duplicating
it, which is the main correctness risk reducer. AttributesToGet on
Query/Scan (the only one of these seven fields with no evaluation-engine
complexity) was fixed separately in this pass; that fix's
resolveProjection()-reuse pattern is a template for the others.

Flagged, not fixed, in gopherstack-rkmp: this is real feature work (new
evaluation surface across 5 operations) with real correctness risk if rushed,
not a quick data-structure change -- same reasoning that deferred the
Global Tables v1 autoscaling gap (gopherstack-l3vv) and initially deferred
the GSI/LSI full-scan perf gap (gopherstack-anlc) until it got its own pass.
notes: Partially fixed 2026-08-14: Expected/ConditionalOperator/AttributeUpdates (PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem) implemented by translating into ConditionExpression/UpdateExpression and reusing the existing expr evaluator -- see legacy_conditions.go and PARITY.md gaps entry. This closes the two most severe failure modes named in this issue (bypassed conditional check, no-op UpdateItem). KeyConditions/QueryFilter/ScanFilter (Query/Scan) remain unimplemented and are tracked separately as gopherstack-yvs8 (discovered-from this issue).
close_reason: Fully resolved across both passes: Expected/ConditionalOperator/AttributeUpdates (PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem) fixed in the original pass; KeyConditions/QueryFilter/ScanFilter (Query/Scan), tracked separately as gopherstack-yvs8 (discovered-from this issue), are now also fixed -- see gopherstack-yvs8 and PARITY.md gaps for the full writeup.

title: cloudformation DeactivateType reads TypeArn where the SDK sends Arn
description:
Found during the 7185 empty-result sweep (002ee3a47) and left unfixed to keep that pass in scope.

handler_type_registry.go handleDeactivateType reads form key TypeArn. The pinned serializer sends Arn - cloudformation@v1.76.1 serializers.go:7751. A caller deactivating a type by ARN, which is one of the two documented ways to identify it, has that value silently dropped.

Same class as ec2's DescribeSecurityGroupRules reading Filter.1.Value: a key the real client never sends, so the parameter is invisible and the op behaves as though it were omitted.

Worth checking the rest of that file while fixing - the type registry family shares parsing helpers and the sibling ops take the same Arn-or-name pair.
close_reason:
Confirmed against cloudformation@v1.76.1 serializers.go: DeactivateTypeInput sends Arn (line 7751), not TypeArn. Fixed handleDeactivateType to read form.Get("Arn").

Checked the rest of the type-registry family (handler_type_registry.go) for the same wrong-key pattern by grepping every form.Get("TypeArn")/form.Get("Arn") call and cross-referencing against each op's real serializer (ActivateType, DeactivateType, DescribeType, DeregisterType, PublishType, SetTypeDefaultVersion, SetTypeConfiguration, TestType, ListTypeVersions, ListTypeRegistrations). Found one sibling with the identical bug: handleActivateType also read TypeArn, but ActivateTypeInput has no such member -- the real ARN identifier is PublicTypeArn (serializers.go:7181). Fixed both.

PublishType/SetTypeConfiguration/ListTypeRegistrations/ListTypeVersions have a different, larger gap (they never read an Arn/TypeArn identifier at all, not a wrong-key read) -- left alone as out of scope for this wrong-key fix; noted but not filed as a new issue since it's a known, lower-value gap already partially documented in PARITY.md.

Added TestTypeRegistry_IdentifyByArn (real aws-sdk-go-v2 client) covering both ActivateType-by-PublicTypeArn and DeactivateType-by-Arn with no TypeName given. Hand-reverted both fixes: DeactivateType failed with TypeNotFoundException (arn resolved to the empty-typeName default key), ActivateType silently created a bogus empty-key registry entry instead of reactivating the real one (test caught it via DescribeType showing IsActivated=false). Restored fix is byte-identical to the original diff.
