   structural PATCH targets, not a competing top-level handler. glacier's
   GetVaultLock is bound only via a switch-case to handleVaultLock (which
   internally calls handleGetVaultLock for that one case), but bindOp's
   handler-name-convention matching finds handleGetVaultLock too and reports
   ambiguity. Both hand-verified as false: the real handler in each case is
   correct.

Sizing: 12 services swept end to end for gopherstack-zquj (swf, iot, emr,
memorydb, lightsail, ram, glacier, mediaconvert, personalize, apigateway,
databrew, dax). Total mismatched-key/unresolved-op noise from these 4 classes
across the 12: several hundred, roughly 90%+ of everything reported. Real
bugs found in the same sweep (NOT part of these classes, fixed already):
services/emr JobFlowExecutionStatusDetail.StateChangeReason ->
LastStateChangeReason tag; services/iot's package-wide error envelope
({\"error\":msg} on ~48 malformed-request 400s, undecodable by any real
client, fixed to {__type,message}); services/iot ListThingGroups items keyed
thingGroupName/thingGroupArn instead of the real GroupNameAndArn shape's
groupName/groupArn; services/iot ListTopicRules items wrote sql (real
TopicRuleListItem has no such member) instead of topicPattern.
close_reason: Closed

title: cmd/keycheck: two new blind-spot refinements found sweeping cognitoidp (lambda-trigger envelope pollution, OpsA/B/C deterministic override)
description:
NOT filed against cmd/keycheck's source because another agent has it locked
for restjson1 path-dispatch work this session (gopherstack-zquj's operating
constraints). Documenting the two findings here so whoever edits
cmd/keycheck/main.go next can fold them into the package doc alongside the
existing blind spots.

1. REFINEMENT OF BLIND SPOT #2 (Lambda-trigger-envelope pollution).
   cognitoidp's auth ops (SignUp, ConfirmSignUp, AdminConfirmSignUp,
   AdminCreateUser, InitiateAuth, AdminInitiateAuth, RespondToAuthChallenge,
   AdminRespondToAuthChallenge, ForgotPassword, ResendConfirmationCode,
   GetTokensFromRefreshToken) each invoke a shared Lambda-trigger-invocation
   helper (lambda_triggers.go) that builds/parses the real AWS Cognito Lambda
   trigger event envelope: version, triggerSource, region, userPoolId,
   userName, callerContext{awsSdkVersion,clientId}, request, response,
   clientMetadata, userAttributes, validationData, autoConfirmUser/
   autoVerifyEmail/autoVerifyPhone (PreSignUp), challengeName/session/
   challengeAnswer/challengeMetadata/challengeResult/answerCorrect/
   publicChallengeParameters/privateChallengeParameters (Define/CreateAuthChallenge/
   VerifyAuthChallengeResponse), issueTokens/claimsOverrideDetails/
   claimsToAddOrOverride/claimsToSuppress/groupOverrideDetails/groupsToOverride/
   iamRolesToOverride/preferredRole (PreTokenGeneration), failAuthentication/
   userNotFound/newDeviceUsed, emailMessage/emailSubject/smsMessage/
   codeParameter/usernameParameter/ConfirmationCode/CustomMessage/
   CustomMessageSubject (CustomMessage). writtenKeys' same-package BFS has no
   way to distinguish "this map literal is the Lambda invocation payload" from
   "this map literal is the op's own HTTP response", so it attributes every
   one of these to the op being checked -- accounting for roughly 250-260 of
   the 304 mismatched keys keycheck reported for cognitoidp pre-triage (~85%
   of the total). A related CASE-MISMATCH false-positive rides on the same
   mechanism: the trigger envelope's lowercase userName/challengeName/session
   keys coincidentally case-collide with the op's OWN correctly-PascalCased
   Username/ChallengeName/Session struct-tagged fields, so the tool reports a
   case mismatch on a key that is actually written correctly elsewhere by an
   unrelated code path.

   A second, narrower instance of the same shape: several ops build an
   internal map[string]string of user attributes (attrs["sub"], attrs
   ["custom:temporaryPassword"], attrs["phone_number_verified"], devices.go's
   attrs["device_name"]) that is later converted via sortedAttributeList into
   a []AttributeType{Name,Value} list -- the map's keys become attribute
   NAME values, never JSON keys, but the BFS can't tell "map feeds a Name/
   Value conversion" from "map is serialized directly".

2. REFINEMENT OF BLIND SPOT #6 (OpsA/OpsB/OpsC deterministic override, not
   true ambiguity). cognitoidp has a package-wide idiom: many op families
   keep BOTH a legacy/simple handler (handle<Op>, bound in an earlier-named
   "OpsA" map) and a hardened "handle<Op>Accurate"/"handle<Op>Full" (bound in
   a later "OpsB"/"OpsC" map), and dispatchTable() merges all of them via
   sequential maps.Copy(table, ...) calls -- Go's maps.Copy overwrites on key
   collision, so whichever Ops-map is copied LAST always wins, deterministically.
   This is not sqs's true ambiguity (two protocol-distinct handlers, neither
   reachable by inspection alone); it's knowable by reading dispatchTable()'s
   call order. bindOp currently has no visibility into that order and reports
   every one of the 27 such ops (AdminSetUserMFAPreference, AssociateSoftwareToken,
   SetUserMFAPreference, VerifySoftwareToken, {Create,Get,List,Update}Group,
   ListUsersInGroup, {Create,Describe,Get,List,Update}IdentityProvider(s),
   {Create,Delete,Describe,List,Update}ResourceServer, {Create,Update}UserPoolDomain,
   {Describe,Set}RiskConfiguration, {Get,Set}UICustomization,
   GetUserAttributeVerificationCode, VerifyUserAttribute) as AmbiguousOps/ERROR,
   masking them from checking entirely under the stale "42 unresolved" framing.
   Hand-resolving all 27 via dispatchTable()'s literal call order and manually
   checking the winning handler found one real bug (adminUserJSON's
   "UserAttributes" tag, fixed this pass) and confirmed the rest clean or
   already-documented (PARITY.md's risk_config LastModifiedDate/domains
   Routing/branding CSSVersion deferred gaps). A safe general fix: when an op
   is bound by two composite literals that are each the return value of a
   distinct zero-arg method call, and dispatchTable() (or an equivalent
   assembly function) calls maps.Copy for each in a fixed textual order,
   prefer the literal whose assembling call is textually LAST -- but this
   needs care to avoid mis-resolving true per-protocol ambiguity (sqs) the
   same way.
close_reason: Closed

title: directoryservice DirectoryVpcSettingsDescription.SecurityGroupId wire key wrong -- also needs synthesis, not a pure tag fix
description:
Real DirectoryVpcSettingsDescription.SecurityGroupId is a single *string (types/types.go:566, deserializers.go:14066 case "SecurityGroupId", directoryservice SDK) -- AWS auto-creates exactly one domain-controller security group per directory. gopherstack's directoryVpcSettingsJSON (services/directoryservice/handler.go:498) emits the internal []string as a plural "SecurityGroupIds" list, a key/shape the real deserializer never matches, so DescribeDirectories' VpcSettings.SecurityGroupId decodes nil on every real client.

NOT a pure tag rename: DirectoryVpcSettings.SecurityGroupIDs (interfaces.go:376) is never populated on any live path today -- CreateDirectory/CreateMicrosoftAD/ConnectDirectory/AddRegion request parsing all omit it entirely (matches real AWS: users never supply it), and nothing else synthesizes a placeholder value the way synthesizeDNSIPAddrs(id) does for DNS. Renaming the wire key alone would leave the field permanently absent (empty slice -> map write skipped), so there is no way to produce a real-SDK-client round trip proving a non-nil decode without ALSO adding synthesis of a fake sg-xxxx value at directory-creation time -- that synthesis is feature work beyond the zquj sweep's tags/keys-only scope. Filing per that constraint rather than shipping an unprovable half-fix.

To close: add a synthesized SecurityGroupID (same pattern as synthesizeDNSIPAddrs) at CreateDirectory/CreateMicrosoftAD/ConnectDirectory time, store it on storedVpcSettings, then change directoryVpcSettingsJSON to emit it as singular "SecurityGroupId". Verify with a real-SDK-client CreateDirectory + DescribeDirectories round trip asserting VpcSettings.SecurityGroupId decodes non-nil.

title: [bug] cmd/keycheck can't resolve 3+ more dispatch-table conventions -- comprehend/personalize/translate/glue/ssm/forecast/dynamodbstreams unswept
description:
gopherstack-zquj's keycheck sweep fixed one dispatch-table blind spot
(const-identifier-keyed map literals, e.g. dms) but found at least three MORE
conventions the tool's findOpDispatch/recordMapDispatch/findHandlerSelector
still can't resolve, all correctly reported as ERROR (fail-loud, never
silently clean) rather than fixed:

1. Bare lowercase method-value dispatch, no "handle"/"json" prefix
   (handleNameRe requires ^(handle|json)[A-Z]): personalize and translate
   both build ops as map[string]opFunc{"CreateDatasetGroup":
   h.createDatasetGroup, ...} -- method names like createDatasetGroup have no
   recognized prefix at all. comprehend is similar (h.detectSentiment,
   h.tagResource, etc., built incrementally via buildOperations()).

2. Wrapped-backend-call / closure dispatch: ssm's ssmDispatchTable() family
   funcs use jsonOp(h.Backend.PutParameter) (wraps a *Backend* method, whose
   name never has a handle/json prefix either) and inline func literals
   (func(ctx, b) (any, error) {...}), neither of which findHandlerSelector's
   AST walk (which looks for a *ast.SelectorExpr matching handleNameRe) can
   match.

3. Ordered-binding-slice dispatch: glue builds its 299-op table from a
   package-level glueOpBindings slice (handler_routing.go), iterated in
   buildOps() rather than a literal map[string]X{...} -- recordMapDispatch
   only inspects CompositeLit map literals with KeyValueExpr elements, not a
   slice of binding structs consumed in a loop.

forecast (operationSpec-struct dispatch) and dynamodbstreams (dispatch shape
not yet characterized) reported HandlerOpsResolved == 0 too and may be a
4th/5th convention -- not yet investigated.

Services currently unswept as a result (all confirmed report
"ERROR: zero op-to-handler dispatch bindings resolved" -- correctly
fail-loud, not silently clean): comprehend (85 SDK ops), personalize (71),
translate (19), glue (299), ssm (152), forecast (63), dynamodbstreams (4).
glue and ssm alone are ~450 unswept ops.

Not fixed in the zquj sweep pass: extending recordMapDispatch/
findHandlerSelector to cover these safely (without loosening the
handle/json-prefix heuristic so much it starts misattributing unrelated maps
as op-dispatch tables, which would trade today's safe fail-loud unresolved
state for a dangerous false-clean one) needs the same test-first,
hand-revert-verified rigor as the const-key fix, one convention at a time.

title: dynamodb: GSI autoscaling settings never echoed on Update/Describe TableReplicaAutoScaling
notes:
Found while fixing gopherstack-1vv2's dynamodb UpdateTableReplicaAutoScaling
clobber bug. types.ReplicaAutoScalingDescription.GlobalSecondaryIndexes
(aws-sdk-go-v2/service/dynamodb/types/types.go:2642) is a real SDK field.

(autoScalingSettings.GlobalSecondaryIndexes, services/dynamodb/store.go) but

title: eks: TestUpdateClusterVersionReturnsInProgress races under -race (pre-existing)
description: Pre-existing data race, not introduced by gopherstack-tp8x. go test ./services/eks/... -race reproducibly races on updates.go:30 (InMemoryBackend.UpdateClusterVersion's scheduleUpdateTransition goroutine writing cl.Status) vs updates_test.go:920 (TestUpdateClusterVersionReturnsInProgress reading it from the test goroutine) -- an unsynchronized read of state a background worker.After() closure mutates concurrently. title: [bug] repeated Updates clobber each other on singleton configs with no Create op
notes:
Split out of gopherstack-1vv2 by the sweep that closed its main scope
(5536d43de), which correctly judged this a DIFFERENT class rather than
folding it in.

1vv2 covers Create-wide / Update-narrow: a handler replaces a stored
structure with the narrower payload a real client's Update type can carry,
destroying the rest. That comparison needs a Create op to compare against.

THIS CLASS HAS NO CREATE OP AT ALL. Singleton configuration resources are
only ever updated:

    appconfig.UpdateAccountSettings
    iam.UpdateAccountPasswordPolicy
    iot.UpdatePackageConfiguration
    iot.UpdateAccountAuditConfiguration
    macie2.UpdateSensitivityInspectionTemplate
    macie2.UpdateClassificationScope
    medialive.UpdateReservation

Confirmed by SDK lookup that no Create* op exists for any of them, so 1vv2's
structural check does not apply and they were excluded from that sweep.

THE SUSPECTED BUG, stated as a hypothesis rather than a finding: several of
these inputs use pointer-optional sub-fields, which is AWS's usual signal for
partial-update semantics -- send only what you want changed. If gopherstack
assigns the decoded payload wholesale, then the SECOND Update wipes whatever
the FIRST one set but the second did not mention. The damage is
Update-versus-previous-Update, not Create-versus-Update.

The 1vv2 sweep flagged appconfig and iot specifically as showing this shape.
Neither was drilled to member level.

THE CHECK: for each op, read the real input type. If its scalars are
pointers (or it has an explicit *Updates/*ForUpdate shape), the contract is
almost certainly partial. Then read the handler's write path: does it merge
field by field, or assign? athena's UpdateWorkGroup in 5536d43de is the
worked example of the merge shape this needs -- a pointer-scalar updates type
with a MergeInto method.

PROOF STANDARD, and it differs from 1vv2's: update field A, then update field
B alone, then assert A still holds its value. A single update proves nothing
here, and neither does create-then-update, since there is no create.

BEWARE THE OPPOSITE ERROR: some singleton configs genuinely are
replace-the-whole-document, and AWS says so in the op's own documentation.
cloudfront's update ops are the precedent -- their docs explicitly require
"the entire continuous deployment policy configuration, including fields you
didn't modify". Read the doc text before assuming a merge is wanted.

Related: gopherstack-1vv2 (parent class), gopherstack-oc9v (found the original).
Cross-ref: 1vv2's receiver-scope sweep (now closed) found dynamodb.UpdateTableReplicaAutoScaling was actually this issue's shape (Update-vs-previous-Update clobber, no Create op to compare against) -- fixed there, see gopherstack-1vv2's closing note and services/dynamodb/PARITY.md autoscaling family. This issue's own remaining scope (medialive.UpdateReservation, appconfig/iot/macie2/ssoadmin already done by c37164f25) is untouched by this pass.

title: kind-mismatch sweep: triage the 526 unknown-key candidates and the securityhub ConnectorV2 shape
description:
gopherstack-g479's map[string]any blind spot (item 3 in its own notes) is now closed by this pass. A new go/types-based scanner (kept in the session scratchpad, not committed -- see below) found map[string]any{} literals and index-assignments across all 145 JSON-protocol services, classified each string-keyed value's real JSON kind via actual type-checking (not text heuristics), and compared against a corrected version of gopherstack-us9u's SDK-side kind table.

6 real bugs fixed this pass, each proven via a real aws-sdk-go-v2 client round-trip test, hand-reverted against the SDK's own error text, restored, md5sum-verified byte-identical:
  eks          DescribeAddonConfiguration.configurationSchema  object -> string (raw JSON schema text)
  eks          DescribeClusterVersions support dates            string -> epoch number (x2 fields, x4 table rows)
  eks          AssociateEncryptionConfig Update.params           object -> array of {type,value}
  opensearch   DescribeDomainHealth counts (4 fields)             number -> string (NumberOfNodes/Shards/AZs shape); also dropped 3 invented keys (ActiveShards/UnAssignedShards/DocumentCount, none real)
  opensearch   DescribeDomainChangeProgress Start/LastUpdatedTime string -> epoch number
  opensearch   DescribeInstanceTypeLimits.MinimumInstanceCount    string -> number
  dms          DescribeEvents.Date                                string -> epoch number
  forecast     GetAccuracyMetrics.Quantile                        string label -> number; TestWindowStart/End string -> epoch number
  inspector2   DescribeOrganizationConfiguration.AutoEnable       bool -> per-scan-type object

Also found and fixed (separate class -- keys nonexistent in the real SDK, reported separately from kind mismatches, same shape as ssm's Patch.State):
  codeartifact DescribePackage emitted domainName/domainOwner/repository, none of which are members of types.PackageDescription at all (confirmed against both deserializers.go and types/types.go). This also corrects a wrong belief a prior pass (gopherstack-6flj) operated under -- its DeletePackage fix's own framing assumed packageToMap (the "Describe shape") was correct and just misapplied; it wasn't.

Real bugs identified but NOT fixed this pass, deferred:
  securityhub ConnectorV2 family (connectorV2ToResponse, shared by Create/Update/GetConnectorV2) emits "Provider" and "ConnectorStatus", neither of which exists on GetConnectorV2Output (real shape has ProviderDetail instead, confirmed against aws-sdk-go-v2/service/securityhub@v1.75.4's deserializers.go). Create/UpdateConnectorV2Output DO have ConnectorStatus but Get does not, and none of the three have "Provider" -- this needs ProviderDetail modeled and the three response builders split apart, a materially larger fix than a kind mismatch. File as its own follow-up.

What the scanner could NOT resolve, needing hand triage next:
  526 "key exists nowhere in the SDK module" candidates (after fixing two false-positive classes discovered in the sdk-side extractor itself: (a) it never captured *_deserializeOpDocument* -- top-level response-body -- functions at all, only nested *_deserializeDocument* ones, which is exactly the level many map[string]any literals sit at, cutting the kind-mismatch bucket from 49 to 37 once fixed; (b) `case "a", "b":` multi-label case lines were silently unmatched by the original single-label regex, bleeding the next case's body into the previous case's classified kind). This 526 bucket is highly likely dominated by generic-key-name collisions across unrelated structs (same class pass1's low-confidence bucket hit) and by services/directories that host multiple SDK modules under one gopherstack package (e.g. services/bedrock implements both the plain bedrock and bedrockagent SDK modules -- a bedrock.tags finding was a false positive purely because the dir->module override table assumes 1 gopherstack dir = 1 SDK module). Needs the same manual per-candidate deserializer confirmation this pass did for the 37, at volume.

Also still open from the original g479 scope, untouched this pass:
  1. The 19 XML/query-protocol services (structurally out of reach for any interface{}-based kind method).
  2. cloudwatch (schema-driven codegen) and appstream (rpc-v2-cbor).

Scanner status: built as a Go tool (go/packages + go/types) at scratchpad's maplitscan/main.go, kept in the session scratchpad only, NOT committed to cmd/. It resolves keys given via literals AND package-level string constants (go/types constant evaluation, not text matching -- the codebase's keyStatus/keyARN-style convention would otherwise silently drop most keys), classifies []byte as base64-string but special-cases encoding/json.RawMessage (re-embeds verbatim, NOT base64 -- misclassifying this as "string" produced 18 false positives in sagemaker before the fix, since RawMessage is exactly how this codebase stores pre-serialized nested-object JSON). Two more Go-side bugs it does NOT yet handle: (a) named types with a custom MarshalJSON whose method body isn't a simple `return json.Marshal(x)` call are left "unknown" rather than resolved -- conservative, not a false-positive risk, but reduces recall; (b) no attempt to determine whether a map[string]any literal ever actually reaches an HTTP response body vs. building some unrelated internal/export-document structure (OpenAPI/Swagger export builders in apigateway/apigatewayv2 produced 5 confirmed false positives this pass since they emit AWS's OAS export format, not a typed SDK response). Both are candidates for hardening before this tool would be trustworthy enough to commit under cmd/.

Refs: gopherstack-g479, gopherstack-us9u
close_reason:
526-candidate unknown-key bucket fully triaged by hand. 34 real fixes made across 16 services (bedrock x3, opensearch x1, bedrockruntime x1, quicksight x5, inspector2 x4, securityhub x3, eks x2, transfer x1, directoryservice x1, codepipeline x1, codecommit x2, elasticsearch x1, mediaconvert x1, backup x1, ce x3, shield x3), each proven via a real aws-sdk-go-v2 client round trip or raw-body assertion, hand-reverted against git show HEAD:<path> to confirm the exact predicted symptom, restored, md5sum-verified byte-identical.

False-positive classes found and documented (the highest-value part of this pass): (1) directory hosting 2+ SDK modules (bedrock/bedrockagent, opensearch/opensearchserverless, personalize/personalizeruntime) -- ~150 candidates; (2) non-SDK surfaces (apigateway/apigatewayv2 OpenAPI export docs, opensearch data-plane, iotdataplane/iot/glacier/apigateway raw-payload-blob ops bound to []byte or io.ReadCloser, cloudwatchlogs event-stream ops) -- ~90 candidates; (3) internal-only structures never reaching an HTTP response (cognitoidp JWT claims/Lambda-trigger-event envelopes ~100 candidates, appsync VTL resolver pipeline, stepfunctions ASL $$ context object, eventbridge delivery envelope, ecs SFN integration); (4) error-envelope fields (__type/code) parsed by shared protocol code, invisible to any per-op deserializer scan (13 candidates); (5) dynamic map[string]T keys (role names, metric names) that are correctly absent from a per-key case-switch by construction (opensearch/elasticsearch LimitsByRole, personalize GetSolutionMetrics); (6) already-fixed-by-a-prior-pass stale scanner snapshot entries (opensearch DescribeDomainHealth, codeartifact); (7) already-documented deliberate SDK-lag disclosures a prior pass had already verified against AWS docs (transfer ContentEncryptionCiphers/HashAlgorithms, directoryservice LDAPSType/UpdateType).

One high-value structural discovery: services/bedrock's AgentsHandler (DataSource/KnowledgeBaseDocuments/Agent CRUD) is registered but its MatchPriority (85) loses to services/bedrockagent.Handler's (87) for every /agents,/knowledgebases,/flows,/prompts path -- confirmed dead code for any real client, same class as opensearch's already-known dead REST-path duplicate. Two fixes were made there before this was discovered; both harmless (already independently correct in the live bedrockagent package), documented in bedrock/PARITY.md, not reverted.

6 confirmed real bugs needing more than a key rename were deferred rather than rushed -- filed as gopherstack-tp8x with the exact fix shape for each: eks kubernetesNetworkConfig/networkingConfig split, pinpoint 3-channel credential-echo (coupled to flag-derivation logic), securityhub GetRecommendedPolicyV2's whole wrong response family, transfer ListFileTransferResults cardinality, guardduty StartMalwareScan's TriggerDetails shape, medialive DescribeInputDeviceThumbnail's header-vs-body confusion.

Not reached, same as before: securityhub ConnectorV2 family, the 19 XML/query-protocol services, cloudwatch (schema codegen), appstream (rpc-v2-cbor) -- carried forward in gopherstack-tp8x.

Gates green on all 16 touched services: go build, go vet, gofmt -l, go test -race, golangci-lint (0 issues) per-service, plus go build ./..., go vet -tags e2e/-tags integration ./... clean. No nolint added. sagemaker (concurrent agent's territory) untouched. Scanner tooling (maplitscan + compare_maplit.py, both Python/Go in the session scratchpad) reused as-is from gopherstack-g479/us9u, not committed to cmd/ -- still has the two documented recall gaps (custom MarshalJSON, map[string]any reachability) plus a newly-observed one (map[string]string literals and for-range-over-map-literal patterns aren't traced, missing the pinpoint APNS leak and 2 of 3 ce RecommendationTotalCount instances, both found by hand instead).

title: gopherstack-us9u kind-mismatch sweep: unreached surface (low-confidence bucket, XML/query services, ad hoc map[string]any construction)
description:
gopherstack-us9u built a mechanical tool comparing the pinned SDK's per-op deserializer-expected JSON kind (parsed from deserializers.go's 'case "key":' + type-switch, for the 145 JSON-protocol services -- restjson1/awsjson1.0/awsjson1.1) against gopherstack's own struct-field-declared kind (parsed from every json-tagged struct field across each service package), matched by exact real-AWS-struct-name correspondence (this codebase's own convention, e.g. ParameterMetadata/PatchStatus/Finding match the real SDK type names exactly). 8 real bugs were found and fixed across codecommit, firehose, appsync, ecr, athena, mediaconvert, pipes, sagemaker (see PARITY.md entries dated 2026-08-21 gopherstack-us9u in each). This issue tracks what the method structurally could not reach, for whoever picks this up next:

1. XML/query-protocol services (19 modules: 14 query, 4 restxml, 1 ec2query) are entirely out of reach for this method -- their generated deserializers decode via reflection into the declared Go SDK struct's own type (not a case+type-switch over a decoded interface{} map), so a kind mismatch there needs a different check (does gopherstack render valid XML for the declared field's Go type), not covered by this tool at all.

2. cloudwatch (schema-driven newer smithy-go codegen, no monolithic deserializers.go with the case-switch pattern) and appstream (rpc-v2-cbor protocol, binary wire format, not JSON at all) use codegen this tool's regex-based extraction doesn't parse. Neither was checked.

3. The comparison tool's gopherstack-side extraction only sees Go struct field DECLARATIONS with json tags. It has two structural blind spots, both encountered repeatedly this pass and resolved by hand every time: (a) a struct whose field is directly marshaled by json.Marshal/echo.JSON vs a same-named domain struct that's actually converted through a separate map[string]any-building handler function before reaching the wire (the tool flags the domain struct's kind, which may be irrelevant if a handler always converts it) -- every 'high confidence' hit this pass needed a manual read of the actual marshal call site to confirm real vs false positive; roughly 190 of the 242 initial hits were false positives from this exact blind spot (sagemaker Tags/CreationTime, ecr resourceTags, ram tags, glue Tags, eks certificateAuthority, cloudwatchlogs status/deliveryDestinationConfiguration, codepipeline trigger, fis timestamps, apigateway/apigatewayv2/fsx/identitystore epoch wrapper types with custom MarshalJSON). (b) fields built entirely inside an ad hoc map[string]any{} literal in a handler function, never appearing as a struct field with a json tag anywhere -- this class (exactly how the original 3 confirmed instances in this issue's notes were found, e.g. inspector2 Finding.Severity) has NO automated coverage at all in this pass; every instance actually fixed this pass was reached via the struct-field path, not this literal-scanning path. A 'Pass 2b' ad hoc map-literal scanner was planned but not built (see us9u session notes) given time budget; building it (grep every 'map[string]any{' / 'map[string]interface{}{' block in every handler_*.go across the 145 in-scope services, classify each string-keyed value expression's kind heuristically, cross-reference against the same SDK kind table) is the highest-value next step to close this gap.

4. The 'low confidence' bucket from this pass's comparison (567 raw hits: same wire key name matched between SDK and gopherstack, but no exact real-AWS-struct-name correspondence found on the gopherstack side) was generated but NOT hand-verified at all -- deliberately out of scope for time budget. It is much noisier than the 242 'high confidence' bucket (generic key names like name/status/arn/id recur across unrelated concepts), but may still contain real instances. A next pass should triage this list the same way: filter obvious false-positive classes (time.Time on domain structs with a sibling *View/*Output/*DTO-suffixed wire type already correct; []byte fields, which Go marshals as base64 string and therefore always match a 'string'-expecting SDK member regardless of the tool's naive 'array' classification -- fix this specific false-positive class in the extraction tool before reusing it, it is NOT a Go-language subtlety this campaign should keep re-discovering by hand), then manually verify remaining candidates against the real deserializer case per gopherstack-us9u's method before fixing anything.

5. Scratch tooling used this pass (extract_sdk_kinds.py, extract_gs_kinds.py, compare.py, check_marshal.py, check_time_helpers.py, showcase.py) was kept in the session scratchpad only, not committed to the repo -- it needs the false-positive fixes noted above (esp. the []byte-as-string kind bug) before it's worth promoting to cmd/ for reuse; as-is it produces too much of the noise item 3/4 describe to hand off as a trustworthy standalone tool.
notes:
2026-08-21: The "ad hoc map[string]any construction" item (item 3 in the
original description) is now closed. A go/types-based scanner (not
committed, kept in scratchpad) found and fixed 6 real kind-mismatch bugs
(eks x3 ops, opensearch x3 ops, dms, forecast, inspector2) plus one
invented-keys bug (codeartifact), all proven via real aws-sdk-go-v2 client
round trips with hand-revert verification against the SDK's own error text.
One more real bug (securityhub ConnectorV2's Provider/ConnectorStatus) was
found but needs a larger fix (ProviderDetail modeling, splitting 3 response
builders) and is deferred. The unverified low-confidence bucket (526
candidates after fixing two bugs in the inherited SDK-side kind extractor
itself -- see gopherstack-y1zn for both) and the securityhub deferral are
split out to gopherstack-y1zn. Items 1 (XML/query services) and 2
(cloudwatch/appstream) remain untouched and open on this issue.

title: dead-typed kind-mismatch fields found by gopherstack-us9u sweep, not fixed (never populated, can't demonstrate a live failure)
description:
gopherstack-us9u's kind-mismatch sweep (SDK deserializer-expected-kind vs gopherstack-emitted-kind, cross-referenced by exact struct name) found several fields with the wrong Go kind that would break a real SDK client's decode IF ever populated with a non-zero/non-empty value -- but every one of them is either never assigned anywhere in the backend, or (mediaconvert Queue.ServiceOverrides) conflates the kind bug with a deeper modeling issue. None currently has a demonstrable live failure (the proof standard this campaign requires), so none were fixed; listing them here so a future pass revisiting these features doesn't have to re-discover the type is wrong.

Confirmed dead (declared wrong-kind, zero assignment sites anywhere in the service, omitempty drops the zero value so it never reaches the wire):
- awsconfig: AggregationAuthorization.CreationTime, ConfigurationAggregator.CreationTime, ConfigurationRecorderStatus.LastStartTime/LastStopTime, ConfigRuleEvaluationStatus.LastSuccessfulInvocationTime/LastFailedInvocationTime/LastSuccessfulEvaluationTime/LastFailedEvaluationTime -- all declared string, real SDK wants epoch-seconds json.Number (deserializers.go: 'expected Date to be a JSON Number, got %T instead'). Structs are constructed but these specific fields are never set in any literal or assignment.
- codebuild: CommandExecution.ExitCode -- declared int32, real SDK wants string ('expected NonEmptyString to be of type string'). Never assigned (StartCommandExecution doesn't set it).
- mediaconvert: WarningGroup.Code -- declared string (already correct kind actually, re-check: Job.Warnings is always []WarningGroup{} empty, so Code is never populated regardless of kind -- low priority, kind was fine, listing only because it surfaced in the sweep).
- sagemaker: ContainerDefinition.ModelDataSource -- declared string, real SDK wants object (awsAwsjson11_deserializeDocumentModelDataSource). No assignment site found anywhere.
- timestreamquery: QueryInsightsResponse.QuerySpatialCoverage -- declared float64, real SDK wants object (awsAwsjson10_deserializeDocumentQuerySpatialCoverage). Never assigned.
- firehose: KinesisStreamSourceDescription.DeliveryStartTimestamp -- declared string, real SDK wants epoch-seconds number. Never assigned (the sibling MSKSourceDescription.ReadFromTimestamp WAS live and IS fixed in gopherstack-us9u; this Kinesis-source sibling field is dead by comparison).
- workspaces: DataReplicationSettings.RecoverySnapshotTime (x2 declarations in interfaces.go) -- declared *time.Time (already correct kind for a real client, only listed because it surfaced as a false-positive during the sweep -- no action needed unless kind is ever found wrong on a closer read).

Deferred (real design gap wider than kind, not fixed pending a scoping decision):
- mediaconvert: Queue.ServiceOverrides -- declared map[string]any, real SDK wants []ServiceOverride (a list of AWS-generated operational messages about queue capacity). Two issues, not one: (1) the kind (map vs array), and (2) ServiceOverrides is NOT a real CreateQueueInput field at all (confirmed via aws-sdk-go-v2/service/mediaconvert types.go: ServiceOverride only appears on the Queue/GetQueue output type) -- gopherstack's createQueueInput accepts it as user input, which the real API does not allow. Fixing kind alone would leave the input-schema bug; fixing both requires deciding whether to (a) reject ServiceOverrides on CreateQueueInput entirely and make Queue.ServiceOverrides always empty (matches real semantics: AWS populates it, not the user), or (b) keep accepting it as a gopherstack-specific testing convenience but wire-correct its output kind. Needs a design call, not a mechanical fix.

If any of these fields is ever wired up to real data (e.g. someone implements aggregation-timestamp tracking in awsconfig, or ModelDataSource support in sagemaker), re-check the kind against the deserializer case cited above before shipping -- these notes exist so that work doesn't reintroduce the exact bug class gopherstack-us9u fixed elsewhere.
close_reason: Knowledge-recording issue by design: it lists dead-typed fields that were deliberately not fixed so a future pass need not re-discover them.

title: [bug] gendocs silently buckets unrecognised PARITY.md status tokens as 'other', under-reporting op health
notes:
Found 2026-08-21 while regenerating docs after r80d batch 20. Sibling of
gopherstack-7o96, which fixed gendocs silently DROPPING block-style op
entries; this is the same failure one level down -- an entry that parses,
carrying a status value the classifier does not recognise.

THE TELL. emrserverless' README moved from "22 (22 ok)" to
"22 (20 ok, 2 other)" after a pass that fixed bugs. Cause: two entries were
written `{wire: ok (fixed), ...}`. cmd/gendocs/model.go's classifyToken
lowercases and matches a fixed vocabulary -- ok, clean, fixed, partial,
partial-, gap, deferred, n, n/a -- and anything else falls to bucketOther.
"ok (fixed)" is none of them, so both ops were counted as neither healthy nor
broken. Corrected in the emrserverless manifest to `wire: fixed`.

REPO-WIDE THERE ARE 17 MORE, in real status positions, after lowercasing:

    partial->ok                     8
    new                             3
    honest-disclosed-limitation     3
    n/a-static                      2
    bug                             1

Each one silently subtracts an op from its service's "ok" count and adds it
to "other". Nobody reading the README can tell whether "3 other" means three
unaudited ops or three typos.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. gendocs now fails loudly on an entry it
cannot parse (gopherstack-7o96). It stays silent on a value it cannot
interpret. That is the same shape as the four silently-under-reporting tools
this campaign has already hit -- gendocs' entry parser, cmd/opcensus, the
struct walk, and a grep-based scope estimate that was entirely false
positives. A tool that accepts input it does not understand and emits a
plausible number is worse than one that errors.

FIX, in preference order:
1. Make an unrecognised status token a hard error, exactly as an unparseable
   entry now is. The vocabulary is small and closed; anything outside it is a
   typo, and 17 existing instances prove it happens.
2. If some of the 17 encode a real distinction the vocabulary lacks --
   `partial->ok` may mean "was partial, now ok", and
   `honest-disclosed-limitation` may want to be `deferred` -- decide
   deliberately whether to extend the vocabulary or normalise the manifests.
   Do not extend it just to silence the error.

Either way the 17 need correcting, and a hard error prevents the next batch
adding an eighteenth. Note the count is only of tokens matched in strict
`{wire: X` or `, errors|state|persist: X` positions -- a looser scan drowns
in note prose, so treat 17 as a floor.

Related: gopherstack-7o96 (block entries), gopherstack-c7s3 (silent-empty
tooling), gopherstack-r80d (the pass that surfaced it).
close_reason: Fixed. Unrecognised status tokens now route through the same doc.Warnings gate gopherstack-7o96 added for unparseable entries, so both classes fail loudly through one mechanism. My filed count of 17 was low and wrong in kind: the real number is 47, because my strict-position grep never looked at families' status field and missed the 'ok (fixed)'/'ok (fixed doc)' class entirely (22 of 47, already in fis/efs/swf). All 12 distinct tokens normalised onto the existing vocabulary with none added — deliberately, since extending it to silence the error would restore the silence. Notable calls: 'ok (fixed doc)' → ok not fixed, because its note says only stale prose changed; 'honest-disclosed-limitation' → ok not deferred, since deferred means not-yet-audited while these are audited, permanent and disclosed under an A grade; 'bug' → gap, surfacing s3's deliberately-unfixed severe finding as a real gap instead of a meaningless 'other'. efs and fis recover 9 ops each, sqs 4. make docs double-run confirmed no-op; stepfunctions byte-unchanged. Three sibling silences recorded not fixed: unvalidated gaps: bd refs, unvalidated last_audit_commit (the gopherstack-33in mechanism), and leaks: status rendering with no vocabulary check.

title: upgrade the golangci-lint pin to 2.13.1 and fix the 109 findings deferred by ht49
notes:
Deferred deliberately by gopherstack-ht49 (5619eabb4), which pinned CI and
`make install-deps` to golangci-lint 2.12.2 to restore determinism and
unblock PRs #2430/#2431/#2432.

THE PIN IS TEMPORARY BY DESIGN. Under 2.13.1, `golangci-lint run` at repo
root reports 109 issues:

    goimports      1
    modernize     50
    nolintlint     7
    nonamedreturns 1
    staticcheck   50

Measured on both versions at repo root, not inferred: 2.12.2 -> 0 issues,
2.13.1 -> 109. Sample finding: test/integration/iotanalytics_test.go:380-385,
SA1019 -- AWS has deprecated the iotanalytics service outright and the SDK
types are marked deprecated accordingly, so that one needs a decision about
the service's future rather than a mechanical edit.

WHERE THEY LIVE MATTERS: all of them are in build-tagged files under
test/integration and test/e2e. That is the same blind spot as
gopherstack-0bpp -- code CI compiles but tooling routinely fails to look at.
Two sweeps broke out-of-service callers there without noticing, and `make
test` never compiles those files at all.

THE WORK: bump GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION in Makefile (both workflows read that
one line, so nothing else needs touching) and fix the findings.

Do NOT //nolint them away, and specifically never for
cyclop/gocyclo/gocognit/funlen -- this repo bans those and the ban is a
standing convention, not a lint rule that can be argued with. modernize and
staticcheck at 50 each are likely mechanical; nolintlint at 7 may reveal
existing nolints that are now unnecessary, which is worth reading rather than
bulk-editing.

Do not silently sit on 2.12.2 forever and treat ht49 as having solved this.
It solved the nondeterminism. These are the findings.

title: [bug] cmd/overwidecandidates: sdkImportRe is anchored on a quote but matched against grep -o output, so module resolution always returns nothing
notes:
Found 2026-08-20 while building cmd/bodyclass for gopherstack-cnhp. Flagged
rather than fixed -- that tool was out of scope for the pass that found it.

cmd/overwidecandidates/main.go:63

    sdkImportRe = regexp.MustCompile(`"github\.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/([a-z0-9]+)`)

The pattern requires a leading double quote, which is correct when applied to
raw Go source. But sdkModsFor (same file, ~line 208) applies it to the output
of a `grep -o`, and grep -o emits only the matched substring -- never the
surrounding quote. Confirmed empirically:

    $ grep -rhoE 'aws-sdk-go-v2/service/[a-z0-9]+' services/dax/*.go | head -2
    aws-sdk-go-v2/service/dynamodb
    aws-sdk-go-v2/service/dynamodb

No leading quote, so FindAllStringSubmatch returns nothing and the function
resolves zero SDK modules for every service that is not in its override
table.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the same failure signature as gopherstack-c7s3 --
a resolution step silently returning empty, producing a result that looks
like a real answer. There a service reported "0 ops" and sat unswept for an
entire campaign because a zero is indistinguishable from a small clean
service. Here the fallback presumably masks it, which is why nobody noticed;
worth checking what overwidecandidates actually reports for a service NOT in
its override table before assuming the output has been trustworthy.

FIX: either drop the leading `"` from the pattern, or apply the existing
pattern to file contents rather than grep output. Prefer whichever matches
what cmd/opcensus now does, since that tool's module resolution was corrected
in the same area on 2026-08-20 (6dfd20f14) and the two should not diverge.

Worth a look while there: whether any OTHER tool in cmd/ shares this
copy-pasted pattern with the same mismatch.
close_reason: Verified 2026-08-28 by reading the code. sdkImportRe is now (?m)-anchored per line and matches grep -o output correctly; the comment documents why.

title: [bug] 20 PARITY.md stamps hold prose placeholders, never a sha — caused by the orchestrator's own no-git constraint
notes:
Surfaced 2026-08-20 by cmd/stampaudit (97a474a93), built for gopherstack-z31a.

THE CLASS. 20 of 160 manifests have a last_audit_commit that is not a sha at
all. They hold prose. The repo-wide survey in gopherstack-z31a missed every
one of them because its grep required a hex value:

    grep -oP '^last_audit_commit:\s*\K[0-9a-f]+'

A non-hex value simply did not match, so those manifests fell out of the
denominator silently. That is the same "a wrong number looks like a right
number" hazard this whole family of issues keeps producing -- the survey
reported 140 manifests carrying a stamp and was right, but never said that 20
more carried something that was not one.

THE VALUES, AND WHY THEY EXIST. The placeholders explain themselves:

  4x  HEAD
  3x  pending (uncommitted this pass -- see git log at merge time)
  2x  pending (agent instructed not to commit; see git log for this pass's commit)
  2x  HEAD   # see git log for this pass's commit
  1x  pending (agent instructed not to run git; set at commit time)
  1x  UNKNOWN_SEE_GIT_LOG   # this pass ran without git access; set on next commit
  1x  PENDING_COMMIT  # working tree not committed by this pass (git use was out of scope)
  1x  PENDING (gopherstack-o31x route-table audit, worked in this session)
  1x  PENDING   # gopherstack-6flj wrapper-key/nested-shape sweep -- orchestrator sets on commit
  ... and the rest in the same shape

THIS IS SELF-INFLICTED, AND I AM PART OF IT. Sweep orchestrators -- me
included, all session -- hand workers a hard constraint that they must run no
git-mutating commands, because the orchestrator owns commits. Several agents
read that as "no git at all" and could not resolve HEAD, so they wrote an
honest note into a field that wants a sha. Then no orchestrator went back and
filled it in. One placeholder literally says "orchestrator sets on commit"
and names this session's campaign; I did not set it.

So the field has three failure modes now, not two:
  1. unreachable sha (140/140, structural, squash-merge) -- gopherstack-z31a
  2. sha older than its own audit date (55/140, authoring defect) -- z31a
  3. never a sha at all (20/160, process defect) -- this issue

FIX, in two parts:
- Mechanical: fill in the 20. They are cheap -- `git log -1 --format=%H` at
  the commit that shipped each pass, recoverable from the manifest's own
  last_audit_date plus git log over that service's directory.
- Process, and the part that stops recurrence: the orchestrator must set the
  stamp when it commits, since it is the only party that knows the sha. Two
  options -- either the brief tells workers to write a known sentinel the
  orchestrator greps for before committing, or the stamp stops being
  hand-written entirely and a tool sets it. The current arrangement asks the
  worker for a value only the orchestrator can know, which is why it fails.
- Worth pairing with z31a's merge-base suggestion: if the stamp should record
  the branch's merge-base rather than HEAD, a worker CAN compute that without
  any git mutation, and the whole hand-off problem goes away.

Verify with: `go run ./cmd/stampaudit` -- the placeholder rows are labelled
`placeholder-value` and counted separately from resolved shas.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] opcensus cannot read ssm and route53resolver op tables — both reported a silent zero and nobody noticed
notes:
Surfaced 2026-08-20 by the error-row work in gopherstack-c7s3 (6dfd20f14).

Both services resolve as `unresolved` -- opcensus finds no operations in
their GetSupportedOperations at all -- and before that fix they rendered as
0/0/0/0, indistinguishable from a small clean service. That is why nobody
noticed. They now render ERROR and sort above the ranking.

WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE BOTH BEING SWEPT. ssm and route53resolver were both
read during the wrapper-key campaign, so their wire surface has been
audited. But the ranked remainder that drove sweep ORDER was computed from
opcensus's L+D+G counts, and for these two it was working from zero. ssm in
particular is not a small service. Any future prioritisation that trusts
this tool will mis-rank them the same way.

WHAT TO DO. Read each service's GetSupportedOperations and find the shape the
AST walker cannot follow. dms's turned out to be map keys that were named
consts rather than string literals, fixed in 6dfd20f14 by resolving
*ast.Ident through the const table -- these two are presumably a third shape
again. The tool already has three tiers (chased / direct / dynamic-fallback)
and a documented pattern for extending the fallback scan.

Check while you are there whether any OTHER service resolves through a tier
that happens to work by luck. The error row only fires on a total failure; a
service that resolves PARTIALLY still reports a plausible-looking number.
That is the same "a wrong number looks like a right number" hazard this whole
class keeps producing, and the campaign hit it twice: dms hid 119 ops behind
a zero, and these two hid theirs behind another.

RELATED: gopherstack-c7s3 (closed, the fix and the corrected root cause),
gopherstack-6flj (the campaign whose ranking this fed).
close_reason: Closed

title: cmd/opcensus resolves the SDK module from the directory name, so aliased services silently report zero ops
notes:
ROOT CAUSE IN THIS ISSUE WAS WRONG. Corrected 2026-08-20 (6dfd20f14).

I filed this claiming opcensus resolves the SDK module from the directory
name. It does not resolve an SDK module at all. The original file has zero
references to go.mod, GOMODCACHE or aws-sdk-go-v2/service; op counting is
pure AST-walking of each service's own GetSupportedOperations table. The
diagnosis fit the symptom and not the code, and I filed it without reading
the tool.

THE REAL DEFECT: the dynamic-fallback tier's whole-package scan recognised
only *ast.BasicLit map keys. dms builds its dispatch table from nineteen
family functions returning map[string]service.JSONOpFunc keyed by named
CONSTS, so every entry was skipped. Fixed by resolving *ast.Ident keys
through the const table, which extractLiterals already did elsewhere in the
same file. dms: 0 -> 130 total, 49 L+D+G.

ALSO WRONG: elb was never broken by this tool. It resolves through the
`direct` tier and always did.

WHAT SURVIVED, and why the issue was still worth fixing: the error-row half.
Two services were ALREADY reporting a silent zero and nobody had noticed --
ssm and route53resolver, both `unresolved`, both looking like small clean
services. They now render ERROR in every column and sort above the ranking
with a banner. A zero meaning "no L/D/G ops" is fine; a zero meaning "not
checked" is the bug, and that distinction is now visible.

**ssm and route53resolver need a look.** Neither is small. They were swept in
the wrapper-key campaign, so their SURFACE was read, but the census could not
see their op lists, which means the ranking that drove sweep order was
working from wrong numbers for both. Worth a separate issue if their
GetSupportedOperations uses a shape the walker still cannot follow.

NINE directory/module aliases found, where this issue knew of two:
  awsconfig      -> configservice
  ce             -> costexplorer
  cognitoidp     -> cognitoidentityprovider
  dms            -> databasemigrationservice
  elasticsearch  -> elasticsearchservice
  elb            -> elasticloadbalancing
  elbv2          -> elasticloadbalancingv2   (previously unrecorded)
  serverlessrepo -> serverlessapplicationrepository
  stepfunctions  -> sfn (plus real secondary dynamodb/s3 imports)
SDK-module resolution is now in the tool as an INDEPENDENT second failure
signal, not as the op-count mechanism I wrongly described.

Tombstones: qldb and qldbsession are skipped, not labelled. Census total is
160, matching the real sweepable population.

KNOWN REMAINING NOISE, deliberately not fixed: the fallback scan over-counts
dms's total by eleven, picking up unrelated map[string]interface{} response
literals. A value-shape filter to remove them regressed appstream, waf,
personalize, comprehend, translate, workspaces and workmail, so it was
reverted. Confined to the `total` column; every L+D+G figure is unaffected.
close_reason: Fixed in 6dfd20f14, with the root cause corrected -- see notes. The defect was a const-keyed map entry gap in opcensus's dynamic-fallback AST walker, not the SDK-module-by-directory-name resolution this issue described (that resolution did not exist). dms 0 -> 130 ops / 49 L+D+G. Unresolved services now render ERROR rather than a silent zero, which surfaced ssm and route53resolver as already-broken. Nine directory/module aliases recorded, where this issue knew two.

title: swf shows a structural defence against the wrapper-key bug class: derive regular keys, don't hand-write them
notes:
A SECOND STRUCTURAL DEFENCE, different mechanism, found in emrserverless
2026-08-20. Worth pairing with swf's derived-keys case because the two cover
different halves of this bug class.

swf's defence: DERIVE the key. Prevents wrong-key bugs where the naming is
regular (40 event types, one rule).

emrserverless's defence: DO NOT RECONSTRUCT THE SHAPE AT ALL. It stores and
echoes each nested config sub-object as an opaque map[string]any keyed by the
AWS wire field name, rather than unmarshalling into a typed Go struct and
re-marshalling on the way out. Consequence: it can only return field names
the caller itself sent. Fabricating a response-only member is not expressible,
and request-only fields cannot leak into a response.

That matters because emrserverless has THREE request/response sibling pairs
(ImageConfiguration/ImageConfigurationInput,
IdentityCenterConfiguration/IdentityCenterConfigurationInput, plus twelve
application-config sub-objects) -- precisely the shape that produced a real
bug in efs the same day, where one Go struct served both directions and
DestinationToCreate's request-only fields rode into the response.

THE TRADE-OFF, stated so nobody adopts this blindly: opaque passthrough also
makes the sweep BLIND. Whatever the client sends round-trips consistently, so
a wrong key inside the passthrough is undetectable by this method -- the same
boundary mediaconvert's JobSettings and appmesh's specs hit. It buys
correctness-by-construction for echo-shaped data at the cost of any ability
to validate it, and it is only correct where the service genuinely is an echo.
emrserverless's response-only members (ImageConfiguration.resolvedImageDigest,
IdentityCenterConfiguration.identityCenterApplicationArn) are consequently
never emitted at all -- disclosed as gaps, and a direct cost of the design.

SO THE RULE IS NARROWER THAN "PREFER PASSTHROUGH":
- Echo-shaped nested config with no server-computed members: passthrough is
  strictly safer than a typed round-trip.
- Anything the server must ADD to (a status, a resolved digest, a computed
  ARN): passthrough cannot express it, and a typed shape checked against the
  SDK is required.
The recommendation from this issue stands unchanged either way -- a test
helper asserting emitted keys against the pinned deserializer's case list
protects both designs and costs no production change.
close_reason: Knowledge-recording issue documenting a structural defence pattern. No action item; retained in history for reference.

title: amplify: TestListArtifacts_ProducedByJobCompletion is flaky (running job briefly has artifacts)
description:
Failed once in CI on an unrelated PR (#2419, job 95125560578, run 31930944354):

  FAIL: services/amplify TestListArtifacts_ProducedByJobCompletion/running_job_has_no_artifacts_yet
  Error: Should be empty, but was [0xc0000c0540]

The subtest asserts a job in RUNNING state has produced no artifacts yet, and found one.

Not caused by that PR: the branch touches zero files under services/amplify (git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD), the test passes 5/5 locally, and main's last three runs are green. Re-running the job cleared it.

Likely an async race - the job completes and produces its artifact between the test's setup and its assertion, so whether the subtest sees RUNNING-with-no-artifacts depends on scheduling. Look for a background completion goroutine driven by wall-clock time rather than an injected clock. Note this repo bans time.Sleep in tests; the fix is probably testing/synctest or making completion explicitly triggered rather than timed.

Low priority - one observed occurrence - but it will keep costing unrelated PRs a CI cycle until fixed.

title: dynamodb: UpdateTable exclusivity check is stricter than AWS documents
description:
countUpdateTableMutations (services/dynamodb/table_ops.go) treats eight fields as mutually exclusive. AWS documents only three.

The SDK's own UpdateTable doc (api_op_UpdateTable.go:17-24, aws-sdk-go-v2/service/dynamodb v1.63.1) says verbatim:

  You can only perform one of the following operations at once:
    - Modify the provisioned throughput settings of the table.
    - Remove a global secondary index from the table.
    - Create a new global secondary index on the table.

Not listed, but treated as exclusive by our check: ReplicaUpdates, SSESpecification, StreamSpecification, DeletionProtectionEnabled, TableClass. A client that legitimately combines any of these with a throughput change gets a 400 from us and a success from real AWS.

This is the same class of bug just fixed for BillingMode, which our check also treated as exclusive even though AWS REQUIRES it alongside ProvisionedThroughput when switching modes ('When switching from pay-per-request to provisioned capacity, initial provisioned capacity values must be set', api_op_UpdateTable.go:60-63). That one was found only because terraform-provider-aws sends billing_mode on every capacity change and the terraform drift suite went red.

The BillingMode half is fixed. The remaining five are untested and unexercised - no client in our suites currently combines them - so this is latent, not observed. Verify each against the SDK before loosening; do not bulk-delete the check.
close_reason: Verified 2026-08-28. countUpdateTableMutations counts only ProvisionedThroughput/BillingMode and GSI updates; the over-strict members were removed from the exclusivity check.

title: codeql (go) / Analyze (go) never reports on this repo
description:
Across four CI runs on chore/queue-2026-08-11, the 'codeql (go)' and 'Analyze (go)' checks have never reported a status. Analyze (javascript-typescript) runs and passes.

Consequence: there is currently NO Go static-analysis coverage in CI, and a request to 'fix any codeql issues' is unanswerable for Go because no Go findings are ever produced. Silent absence reads as 'clean' - that is the dangerous part.

Investigate: is the Go matrix leg failing to start, filtered by a path filter, or timing out on a 162-service module? Check .github/workflows for the CodeQL config.

comments.author: Witness Patrol
comments.text:
CORRECTION — the premise of this issue as filed is WRONG. I filed it, and I was wrong on three counts.

1. "codeql (go) never reports" — false. Verified: run 31893253913, job codeql (go), conclusion SUCCESS, 15:38:09Z -> 15:57:37Z (19m28s).
2. "No Go static-analysis coverage in CI" — false. code-scanning/analyses shows /language:go SARIF uploads landing continuously against refs/pull/2417/merge, most recently 16:19:19Z and 16:16:44Z on 2026-08-15.
3. "The prior standalone-CodeQL issue is closed" — false. gopherstack-m8mg is OPEN, P3, filed 2026-07-11, never actioned.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY HAPPENING: ci.yml's codeql job (lines 135-162) takes ~19.5 minutes and lives in a workflow with concurrency.cancel-in-progress: true. During rapid iteration this branch was receiving pushes every 3-7 minutes, so nearly every codeql (go) run was CANCELLED before finishing. Adjacent runs 31895063602 and 31894903224 both show conclusion=cancelled. Sampling four consecutive runs mid-iteration caught it cancelled every time, which is indistinguishable from "never reports" if you do not look at the conclusion field.

My own push cadence was cancelling the check I was reporting as missing.

Meanwhile Analyze (go) / Analyze (javascript-typescript) come from a SECOND, GitHub-managed default-setup workflow (event: dynamic, workflowName: CodeQL, no file in the repo). It is not subject to ci.yml's concurrency policy, so it completes reliably. That is the duplication gopherstack-m8mg is about.

OPEN CODEQL ALERTS: zero. The single open code-scanning alert is #246, tool=Scorecard, rule=Vulnerabilities — not CodeQL. Go CodeQL has produced real findings historically (dismissed alert 254, cognitoidp SRP, tracked in gopherstack-ylyb).

REDUCED TO P3 and re-scoped: this is not "Go analysis is missing". It is the same repo-settings duplication as gopherstack-m8mg, plus a real but lesser annoyance — a 19.5-minute job under cancel-in-progress will almost never complete on an actively-pushed branch, so it burns runner time and yields a cancelled required check. Options: drop ci.yml's codeql job in favour of default setup, disable default setup in repo settings, or move the codeql job to its own workflow without cancel-in-progress. Repo-settings/config decision, not agent-fixable.

One unresolved discrepancy, flagged rather than smoothed over: gh api code-scanning/default-setup returns {"state":"not-configured"}, which contradicts the live evidence of a default-setup workflow running. Most likely the token lacks the scope and returns a placeholder. Not verified either way.

title: resume or discard the stashed directoryservice and opsworks sweeps
description:
Two 6flj passes were killed mid-edit by an API session limit on 2026-08-15. Their work is in a git stash, message 'wip: killed by session limit'.

STATE, verified before stashing:
- services/directoryservice does NOT compile. It was mid-refactor, splitting handleDeleteADAssessment off a shared two-field handler, with an unused context import left behind. Roughly 18 files touched.
- services/opsworks builds but FAILS its tests - TestElasticIps/RegisterElasticIp_without_StackId_returns_400 got 200. Ten files plus a new opsworks SDK dependency in go.mod. The agent's last words were that it was about to verify each fix against unfixed code, so nothing had been hand-reverted yet.

Neither meets this campaign's bar: every fix hand-reverted individually and confirmed to fail with the predicted symptom. Both were stashed rather than committed, and rather than discarded, because the findings themselves may be real.

THE OPSWORKS FAILURE IS AMBIGUOUS and that is the reason to look rather than assume. A test expecting 400 and getting 200 is either the agent breaking an existing test, or a NEW test correctly failing because it had just found a missing validation and had not yet fixed it. Those are opposite conclusions and telling them apart needs the diff read.

RECOMMENDED: do not resume from the stash. Re-sweep both services fresh, and use the stash only as a hint about where to look. Resuming someone else's half-finished refactor is worse than starting clean, and the remainder file already treats both as unswept so nothing is lost by redoing them.

Drop the stash once that judgement is made either way - a stale stash is worse than none.
close_reason:
Both services re-swept fresh. The stash can be dropped.

opsworks: 4 bugs fixed and committed in 0f5a7d360. directoryservice: 6 bugs fixed and committed in 78517e30d.

THE AMBIGUOUS TEST IS RESOLVED, and it was the favourable reading.
RegisterElasticIp_without_StackId_returns_400 does NOT exist at HEAD, so the killed session had written a NEW test that correctly failed on a validation gap it had found and not yet fixed - it had not broken a pre-existing test. Settled by grepping HEAD rather than inferring. The underlying bug is real: RegisterElasticIpInput declares ElasticIp and StackId required and has no Region member, while gopherstack accepted a fabricated Region and never checked StackId.

BOTH RE-SWEEPS WERE DONE FRESH, with the stash read read-only as a hint only. That was the right call. For directoryservice, five of the stash's hints pointed at real bugs but all were independently re-derived, and one bug - DescribeSettings emitting the request-side filter name Status where the real member is RequestStatus - was found this pass and is NOT in the stash. Resuming would have inherited an uncompilable mid-refactor and still missed that.

The dependency boundary the stash had crossed was also restored: it had added the opsworks SDK to go.mod. The fresh pass confirmed the module is in the cache but absent from go.mod, cited the cached source for every wire claim, and disclosed a 0-of-74 real-client test ratio rather than taking the dependency to make its tests easier.

Nothing in the stash is needed. Drop stash@{0} whenever convenient - it is now purely a record of an interrupted session.
